#### §10: Mathematics

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-10.1 | §10.0 | HIST | One generic implementation per operation. Formats that coincide are exported as aliases of one function (C3). |
| D-10.2 | §10.0 | HIST | **Internal:** `(value, Status)` with IEEE flags. No errno. **Boundary:** errno is set per `math_errhandling` (`MATH_ERRNO \| MATH_ERREXCEPT`, kept). This is the only place math touches errno. |
| D-10.3 | §10.0 | — | Accuracy: correctly rounded where the contract requires it. For every other function, a documented ULP bound per function and format is established by the phase-M tests, and it must be at least as tight as the published bounds OD-1 records. **Owner addition (2026-10-05):** coefficients and tables are generated by project tooling (minimax or Remez fitting, high-precision evaluation) with the derivation recorded, never recalled from glibc's source (which is not read). Goal: results identical to glibc's wherever glibc is correctly rounded or the function is exact; elsewhere within glibc's documented error bound and as close to its output as the algorithms allow. Per function and format, the fraction of a large random sample plus the hard-case corpus on which Liella is bit-identical to glibc is measured; each mismatch is classified with the test oracle (glibc not correctly rounded, or a Liella error) and the table is recorded in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`. glibc's particular approximations are not reproduced; a program found to depend on glibc's exact last bits is an owner ruling. |
| D-10.4 | §10.1, §10.3 | HIST, PATH | `isinf` returns ±1 (contract). `signgam` is an exported data symbol written by the `lgamma` translation. The internal `lgamma` returns `(value, sign)`. |
| D-10.5 | §10.6 | HIST, COMPAT | `fenv` keeps MXCSR and x87 in step. `__fpu_control`/`__setfpucw` set the startup x87 word. `__fpu_control` (GLIBC_2.2.5, 2-byte object, 0x037f) is its own csys member (`fpu_control.c`), so a static program that defines the name links; start-up applies a program's own value only in dynamic programs, as glibc (#810, #812, probe-settled). Proven now: export, archive member, static conformance (default and program-defined) and the glibc oracle of the dynamic programs. The dynamic hook's run on Liella and its "drop the hook" plant wait for Liella's ld.so (phase 14, #814); until then that run is a reported skip. |
| D-10.6 | §10.0 | COMPAT | `matherr` and `_LIB_VERSION` are inert compat symbols. |
| D-10.7 | §10.0 | — | **Products.** `crates/libm-so` links `liella-boundary` with feature `libm` (the math exports only) into a static library; `cargo xtask so` turns it into one relocatable object (unused sections dropped from the exports as roots), keeps only the math names global and archives it as `libm.a`, so its private copies of library code never collide with `libc.a`. Names glibc exports from both libraries (`frexp`, `ldexp`, `modf`, `scalbn`, `copysign`, `finite`, `__finite*`, `__signbit*`) are in both products, weak in `libm.a` (a static link takes `libc.a`'s). Rust's `compiler_builtins` carries weak hidden copies of some C math names, made local first so they cannot hide the exports. `libm.so.6` is linked from the object against `libc.so.6` with the version script of `libm.so.6`'s default versions; it cannot be loaded until phase 14. The math code never allocates (the build checks that `libm.a` holds no heap) and the product's panic handler prints a fixed diagnostic and aborts. Compat-only versions wait for phase 15. |
| D-10.8 | §10.0 | HIST | **Exports are generated** (`cargo xtask math-gen`): one body per family in `crates/boundary/src/posix/s10_math.tsv`, expanded over the default versions of `spec/abi/versions.tsv` and the C signatures of `spec/abi/prototypes.tsv` into `posix/s10_math_gen.rs`; symbols with `long double`/`_Float128` values get C forwarders (`csys/src/adapter/math_{libc,both,libm}.c`, OD-C4) compiled into the product that owns them. The environment (§10.6) is hand-written (`posix/s10_math.rs`). |
| D-10.9 | §10.0, §10.4 | — | **One soft-float core.** Every correctly rounded operation computes exactly (256-bit intermediates) and rounds once into the result format, so narrowing is the same code as `fma`. The rounding direction is an argument (C2), read by the translation from MXCSR (x87's control word for `long double`); x87 precision control is not honoured (results are always rounded to 64 bits; decided, reported). Flags travel in `Status` and are raised by `fpu::raise` (set in MXCSR; an SSE operation when the trap is enabled, which delivers `SIGFPE`); `feraiseexcept` sets overflow, underflow and inexact in the x87 status word as glibc does. Hardware `sqrt`/`fma` paths are for the optimization pass. |
| D-10.10 | §10.0–§10.2 | — | **glibc's observable conventions are matched** where the contract leaves them open and the result is exact (`spec/behaviour/libm-exact.md`): the default NaN's sign, which operand's NaN payload propagates (per function and format), `ERANGE` only for ±∞/±0 results, `lrint` of `_Float128` saturating, `fromfp`'s clamped values, the `fmin`/`fmax` choice between ±0, `significand`'s flags per format. Deliberate differences (predicates return 1; x87 unnormals are not finite; pseudo-denormals are canonicalized; `scalbl(NaN, −∞)`) are in `docs/differences-from-glibc.md`. |
| D-10.11 | §10.1 | — | Classification decodes through an optimisation barrier (`float::decode_opaque`): the compiler may otherwise turn bit tests back into floating comparisons, which raise invalid for a signalling NaN. |
| D-10.12 | §10.0 | — | **Oracle and tooling** (D-10.3): `crates/mathtools` (test and tool code; no product depends on it): arbitrary-precision arithmetic with correct rounding by Ziv's strategy, the Remez tool (`cargo xtask remez`, fit files in `crates/math/fits`, generated coefficients with their derivation in `crates/math/src/coeffs`, `--check` regenerates), and the measurement harness (`cargo xtask mathcmp FUNC FMT`: glibc and Liella built from one probe, bit-identical fraction, correct rounding and ulp error of each side against the oracle; exhaustive for `float`). The published bounds are `spec/abi/libm-ulps.tsv` (from the manual, `spec/tools/libm_ulps.py`). |
| D-10.13 | §10.3 | — | **Elementary functions of `float` and `double`** (milestone 2). Evaluated in double-double arithmetic (`math::dd`: error-free sum and Dekker product, no FMA) and rounded once from the exact sum of the two parts (`dd::round`, with the sign of the neglected remainder deciding ties and directed modes), so every result is correctly rounded in every mode; the binary32 forms run the same code on widened operands. The computation needs round-to-nearest: the translation (`mathret::elem`) switches MXCSR to its default for the call, restores it and raises the result's flags. Algorithms: table-driven `exp` (k·ln2/64), `log` (12-bit reciprocal table and an `atanh` series), `pow` as `exp(y·log \|x\|)` with exact powers detected, Payne–Hanek reduction for trigonometric arguments of 1500 and above (Cody–Waite below), `atan` by an `atan(j/64)` table, the hyperbolic functions from `expm1`/`exp`/`log1p` arranged without cancellation, `hypot` exactly in 256 bits in every format. Tables and series coefficients come from the oracle (`cargo xtask tables`, `crates/mathtools/src/tables.rs`, 400-bit evaluation; `--check` in the gate); no Remez fit was needed at this precision. Arguments where the second-order term is far below the double-double error (below 2^-30) or the function has saturated are rounded by the side of the deviation (`elem::near`). The `double` fast paths' result assembly (MATH-M6-F64-GAP-ASSEMBLY, register 13.5 #1 and #6) uses Fast2Sum where the magnitudes are ordered: `exp_kernel` forms `t + t·p` from one exact product and two Fast2Sums; the logarithms add `e·ln2` (a 42-bit `LN2H`, so `e·LN2H` is exact for `\|e\| < 2^11`, plus `e·LN2L`), `−ln c` and `log1p r` by Fast2Sum/2Sum and one low-part sum (`fast64::log_assemble`, below `2^-95·\|e\| + 2^-103` beside the series tail); `log_pow` takes `rh³/3` from the exact `rh²·rh` times the `double` 1/3 with one correction (`< 2^-115·\|rh\|`) and charges `2^-94·\|e\| + 2^-100` for the assembly. The bounds are restated term by term in `fast64.rs` and checked against the multi-precision oracle by its `bounds` unit tests. Measured (MATH-M6-F64-GAP-ASSEMBLY-2, on an AVX2-capable x86-64 build host, instructions:u per call, default and without AVX2 alike): exp and exp2 -24, log, log2 and log10 -60, pow -122; no row slower. The fast paths' argument reduction (MATH-M6-F64-GAP-EXP-REDUCE, register 13.5 #2): `exp` and `pow` subtract `k·ln2/64` with a three-part Cody–Waite constant of 36-, 35- and 34-bit parts (`fast64::reduce_ln2`; every `k·Ci` exact for `\|k\| < 2^17`), `x − k·C0` exact by Sterbenz, one Fast2Sum for `−k·C1`, the low part from `k·C2`, a renormalizing Fast2Sum, and no trailing `x.lo` add for `exp` (`pow` adds its `z.lo` there); both Fast2Sums are exact by the exponent condition, so tiny `r` next to multiples of ln2/64 is covered. `exp2` forms `r·ln2` by Dekker with `ln2` pre-split (`LN2A`/`LN2B`, `fast64::ln2_times`). Bounds, restated term by term in `fast64.rs`: `exp` r within 2^-106.5, `pow` within 2^-96.9, `exp2` within 2^-104·\|r\|, all inside the kernel's 2^-90; checked against the oracle by `fast64::bounds::exp_reduction_stays_within_its_bound` and `exp2_product_stays_within_its_bound`, each bound planted one bit loose and caught. `exp10` and the accurate path keep `exp_log::reduce`. `log2`/`log10` (MATH-M6-F64-GAP-LOG-TABLES, register 13.5 #7) assemble from `LOG2_L`/`LOG10_L` (-log_b c_i, double-double within 2^-104, generated by `cargo xtask tables`) and `LOG10_2_E` (log10 2 as 42 bits plus the rest, within 2^-97): `e·log_b 2 + (-log_b c)` exact by Fast2Sum, only `log1p r` scaled by one exact product `lh·(1/ln b)` instead of a final `Dd::mul`; bound `2^-49·\|T\|·scale + 2^-70·\|y\|` (`scale` the least double >= 1/ln b), restated term by term at `fast64::logb_assemble`; the near test keeps `RHO_LOG = 2^-69` where `\|y.hi\|` >= the least double >= 0.34·scale. Checked by `fast64::bounds::log_tables_cover_their_bounds` and the kernel oracle test; each constant and a table entry planted one ulp off and caught. |
| D-10.14 | §10.0, §10.3 | — | **Flags and `errno` of the elementary functions.** Inexact is raised exactly when the result is inexact, underflow when the rounded result is tiny and inexact (after rounding, x86), overflow as IEEE 754 defines it. glibc omits inexact for tiny arguments of `sin`, `tan`, `asin`, `atan`, `cos`, `acos`, `cosh`, `atan2` and raises it for some exact results (`cbrt(27)`, `log2(2^k)`, `pow(3, 4)`); C leaves both unspecified (F.10), so Liella follows IEEE 754 (decided, reported). Invalid, division by zero, NaN signs (positive domain NaN for `asin`, `acos`, `log10`) and NaN payload choice (`atan2`: `x`'s) follow glibc (D-10.10). `errno` follows §10.0 (`ERANGE` only for ±∞/±0 results); glibc also sets it for some subnormal and largest-finite results of `exp`, `exp2`, `exp10`, `pow` and not for others (three-way: the spec and C's implementation-defined rule against an inconsistent probe: the spec is kept and the difference recorded). |
| D-10.15 | §10.3 | — | **Special functions of `float` and `double`** (milestone 3). Evaluated in a 384-bit binary floating point of the library's own (`math::mp`: truncating add, multiply, division by small integers, Newton reciprocal and square root, `exp`, `ln`, `sin`/`cos` with Payne–Hanek reduction) and rounded once, so every result is correctly rounded in every mode: the series of `erf`, the `1 − erf` and continued-fraction forms of `erfc`, Stirling's series with argument shifting and reflection for `lgamma`/`tgamma` (exact factorials at small integers), and for the Bessel functions the power series below 100 (at most about 150 of the 384 bits cancel), Hankel's expansion above for orders up to √x, forward recurrence for `Y_n` and for `J_n` with `n < x`, Miller's normalised backward recurrence for `J_n` with `n ≥ x` (recurrences beyond 5000 steps in double-double). Constants (π, ln 2, γ by Brent–McMillan, ½ln 2π, 2/√π, 1/√π, 2/π, 130 Stirling coefficients from exact Bernoulli numbers) from `cargo xtask tables`. The oracle uses independent methods where it can (Spouge's formula for `lgamma`, the continued fraction with bracketing convergents for `erfc`). Tiny arguments whose deviation from a representable value lies beyond 384 bits (`erfc(tiny)`, `j0(tiny)`, `j1(tiny)`, `tgamma(±2^-k)`) are rounded by the side of that deviation. |
| D-10.16 | §10.3 | HIST | **Conventions of the special functions follow glibc** (`spec/behaviour/libm-special.md`): positive domain NaNs for `tgamma`, `y0`, `y1`, `yn`; the sign of Γ(x) stored by `lgamma`/`gamma` in `signgam` and `__signgam` (both data objects of `libm`, written by the translation; `lgamma_r` only through its pointer), including −1 for `lgamma(−0)` and 1 at the poles and NaNs; zero limits of the Bessel functions with the sign of their symmetries, `yn(−1, +∞)` = −0. Flags and `errno` as D-10.14. |
| D-10.17 | §10.5 | — | **Complex functions of `float` and `double`** (milestone 4a, `math::complex`). Each part is evaluated in `math::mp` (384 bits) from formulas without cancellation and rounded once, so each part is correctly rounded in every mode: `cexp`, `csin`/`ccos`/`csinh`/`ccosh` as products of the real functions of the parts; `clog` as ½ ln(1 + (x² − 1 + y²)) near \|z\| = 1; `csqrt` by `√((\|z\| + \|x\|)/2)` placed by the sign of x; `ctanh`/`ctan` as `(sinh x cosh x + i sin y cos y)/(sinh² x + cos² y)`, the real part as ±(1 + δ) far out; the inverse functions by Hull, Fairgrieve and Tang's decomposition (`A − 1`, `A − \|x\|` as sums of positive terms); `catanh` with the larger part paired with the 1. New `mp` kernels: `ln1p`, `atan`/`atan2`, `sinh_cosh`, `sin_cos` of any argument, `sin_cos_pi`, `exact_sqrt`, exactness-tracked `mul_x`/`add_x`. Exact parts are recognised: exact square roots (120-bit candidates), \|z\|² = 10^m for `clog10`, small integer powers of `cpow` by exact multiplication, `cpow` of a base on an axis or a diagonal (the only bases whose argument is a rational multiple of π) by exact reduction of the angle, z^½ as `csqrt`. Where a part is a short dyadic number to within 2^-300 (both parts below 2^-150, \|z\| next to 1, \|x\| = 1 beside a tiny y, one part negligible beside the other with an exact root), the leading-order expansion gives the side of the deviation (`Part::Dev`). Known limit: a short dyadic part beside a negligible correction in the remaining asymptotic regimes (for example `catanh(2^-100 + i·2^200)`, whose real part is 2^-500·(1 − 2^-400 + ...)) may be one unit off in a directed mode; a wider fallback precision is the remedy (handoff). (M6-10, MATH-M6-CPLX-DIRECTED: Ziv's ladder below is that remedy; for `float` and `double` every part on a grid of part exponents over the format's range, both significands 1 and 1 + ulp, in all four modes, is the oracle's correct rounding (`complex_directed.rs`); the `long double` and `_Float128` grids are open findings, ignored there until a follow-up decides them.) The oracle (`liella_mathtools::cplx`) uses different formulas (from `hypot` and the real oracles, with error bounds; cpow with absolute bounds through the exponent and angle). **Long double (M5-2, MATH-M5-CPLX-LD-1):** `cexp`, `clog`, `clog10`, `cpow` and `csqrt` (`l` and `f64x`, and `__clog10l`) run on the same core for any `Float` behind C forwarders (D-10.21); a part enters `Mp` from the decoded significand and is rounded once into the format. Cut-offs: the short-dyadic test is `TINY_EXP = -150` (derived for significands up to 73 bits; `derived_for::<F>()` asserts `PREC <= 73` at compile time, so `_Float128` derives its own in M5-4); the exact-root candidate is `max(120, 2·PREC + 2)` bits (#860: x87 `(1 + i(2^64 − 1))²` has a 127-bit \|z\|); `cpow`'s angle reduction is an exact mod 2 (#861: "above 2^56 is even" was wrong for 64-bit significands). The trigonometric, hyperbolic and inverse functions stay on `Small` until M5-3. Proof: `complex_ld_cr_products.rs` (grid over the x87 exponent range in every mode, random lines, the oracle on every differing line; its oracle needs up to 2^16 bits for parts 2^-32891 from a short dyadic value). Known limit (#859): `cpow` whose exponent or phase product exceeds about 2^(370 − PREC − 10) (x87 about 2^296, `double` about 2^307) while the result is still representable is not correctly rounded within 384 bits; no correct-rounding claim is made in that regime, and the remedy is the wider multi-precision work (M5-W `MATH-M5-MP-WIDE` or a follow-up). **Ziv's step, `ln` (MATH-M5-CPLX-F128-ZIV-B1-2, #1912):** every `ln` on the complex `_Float128` Ziv path is `mp::ln_atanh` (atanh series, `mp_kernels`, both widths; also inside `ln1p` and `ln10`), whose absolute error is proven below `2^(max(e_ln, 0) + 12 − B)` for a result below `2^e_ln` (`B` = 384 or 768; proof in its documentation, 8 bits proved plus 4 of margin). Chosen over a proof of the Halley `mp::ln` because its bound needs only the operation bounds; the Halley form serves no Ziv step. Proven bounds so far: `clog`/`clog10` real parts (relative `2^(26−B)` near `\|z\| = 1` through `ln1p`, else `2^(14−B)`; `/ln 10` one bit more), `carg10` `2^(15−B)`, `cpow` of a base on an axis (run-time bound); the inverse functions and `csqrt` (B1-3: first-order counting lemma, `ln1p_class`). **Ziv's step, run-time bounds (MATH-M5-CPLX-F128-ZIV-B2):** the regimes whose error grows with an operand (`cexp`, the products of `csinh`/`ccosh`/`csin`/`ccos`, `ctanh`/`ctan` both sides of \|h\| = 24, `cpow` on an axis, a diagonal, in general and the quotients of a negative integer power) carry each intermediate as an `Approx` (value, exponent of a proven absolute error bound) through the `mpw` header's operation bounds: `exp`'s relative `2^(14−B)·(\|k\| + 64)`, `sinh_cosh`'s `2^(17−B)·(\|k\| + 64)`, `sin_cos`'s `(\|x\| + 2)·2^(4−B) + 2^(9−B)` (Payne–Hanek `2^(11−B)` beyond 2^29), the turn reduction of a phase beyond 2^40 (`2^(ex φ + 8 − B)`), and `e^(x + δ)`'s linearisation for `\|δ\| <= 1/8`. Where no bound can be given (a larger argument error, a divisor whose sign is uncertain, the sign of `ctanh`'s δ uncertain) the part is undecided at that width, never guessed. Every general part of the 18 names is now rounded by Ziv's test on a proven bound (no unproven site is left): 384 bits, then 768, then 1536 (`mpx`) and 3072 bits (`mpy`), entered through cold functions (`complex::ladder`); a part undecided at 3072 bits is that value rounded once and counted (`complex::residual()`) (ZIV-C, rulings #1719/#1758: every step proven; the one assumption is that no binary128 input needs more than 3072 bits). Above 768 bits the Newton counts of `recip`/`sqrt` follow `B` (`NEWTON`: 5 at 1536, 6 at 3072), the 2/π table holds 312 words (`reduce_wide` at `e ≤ 16 383` with `RW = LIMBS + 3`), and every bound gains `log2(B/768) + 1` bits (`WIDTH_SLACK`) for the series that take up to `B/768` times as many terms. The loop ends: it has at most these steps, and exact values are recognised before the test (exact roots, exact quotients of 120 bits, axis and diagonal angles, `Part::Exact`/`Dev`/`Near`/`Zero`); the remaining parts of nonzero finite operands are transcendental (Lindemann–Weierstrass), so no exact boundary is ever approached by them. Known limit (#1905): `cpow` with huge \|c\|, \|d\| (E or Φ near 2^1000, cancelling) is not decidable at 768 bits; the ladder decides it at 1536 or 3072 bits (it starts at 384 like every function; choosing the start from the exponents of c and d would only save the narrower evaluations). Trigonometric factors of a tiny operand (ZIV-C Step 0, 2026-11-04): below `2^(−B/2)` the sine is the operand with the relative Taylor bound `2^(2e − 1)` and the cosine 1 within `2^(2e − 1)` (`small_trig`, also for `cpow`'s angle with its own bound); the absolute `2^(10 − B)` bound had left every part with a subnormal or minimum-normal sine argument undecided at both widths (2219 of 84 308 accuracy-suite calls of `cexp`, `csinh`, `ccosh`, `csin`, `ccos`, `ctan`, `ctanh`), and after it none is undecided at 768 bits (105 calls retried at 384, 9-18 per family). |

| D-10.19 | §10.3 | — | **Elementary functions of `long double`** (milestone 5a, `math::wide`, generic over `Float` so that `_Float128` can reuse it). Each function is evaluated in `math::mp` (384 bits) and rounded once, so every result is correctly rounded in every mode: `exp`, `exp2`, `exp10`, `expm1` by `mp::exp`; the logarithms by `mp::ln`/`ln1p`; `sin`, `cos`, `tan` with the argument reduced in 384 bits below 2^29 and by Payne–Hanek above (`mp::reduce_wide`, any significand up to 113 bits over the whole exponent range; the binary64 reduction now calls it); the inverse and hyperbolic functions from `mp::atan`, `sinh_cosh`, `ln1p` in forms without cancellation; `cbrt` by Newton's iteration; `pow` as `e^(y·ln\|x\|)`. Exact results are computed exactly: powers of two (`exp2`, `log2`), powers of ten (`exp10` of 1..55, `log10` of 10^0..10^27), perfect cubes, and every `pow` whose result is a dyadic number of at most 128 bits (`y = m/2^k` with `k <= 6`, `m <= 200`: exact square roots, then an exact power; powers of two to any integral exponent). Arguments whose deviation from a representable value is below a quarter of its last place (`\|x\| < 2^-34` for the cubic ones, `2^-67` for the linear ones, `tanh` beyond 23.45, `expm1` below −50.8, `pow` with `\|y·ln\|x\|\| < 2^-67`, `atan2` with `\|y/x\| < 2^-72` from the exact quotient) are rounded by the side of the deviation. Dispatch: the trait `math::real::Real` (one method per function, implemented for `f32`/`f64` by the double-double code of D-10.13 and for `F80` by `wide`) is what the single body per family in `s10_math.tsv` calls. Conventions as glibc's `long double` forms (`spec/behaviour/libm-elem-ld.md`): the domain NaN of `logl` and `log2l` is positive (unlike `log`, `log2`), `acosl` returns a NaN operand with its sign cleared. Flags and `errno` as D-10.14. **`_Float128`** (milestone 5, M5-5 `MATH-M5-F128-ELEM-1`): `Real` is implemented for `F128` by `wide` too; `expf128`, `exp2f128`, `exp10f128`, `expm1f128`, `logf128`, `log2f128`, `log10f128`, `log1pf128`, `powf128` and `cbrtf128` are exported; M5-6 `MATH-M5-F128-ELEM-2` exports the rest: `sinf128`, `cosf128`, `tanf128`, `sincosf128`, `asinf128`, `acosf128`, `atanf128`, `atan2f128`, `sinhf128`, `coshf128`, `tanhf128`, `asinhf128`, `acoshf128`, `atanhf128` (Payne–Hanek up to `FLT128_MAX` by `mp::reduce_wide`, checked in s10_3_c_r4). Re-derived for 113 bits: the complete over/underflow cut-off of `e^v` is now (EMAX + PREC + 2)·ln 2 per format (11401.6 for x87, 11435.6 for `_Float128`, whose subnormals reach e^-11433 — the old fixed ±11400 would have flushed them; `exp`, `exp2`, `exp10`, `pow`); `exp10` is representable for 1..48 (5^48 < 2^113) and rounded exactly for 49..55; `log10` exact for 10^0..10^48; `pow` exact for 113-bit odd parts by the same rule (3^71 exact, 3^72 rounded exactly); cubes exact up to 120-bit roots; the tiny-argument cut-offs follow from `PREC` (2^-58 cubic, 2^-116 linear, `expm1` below −85.1). Conventions settled by probe (`elem_f128_products.rs` against glibc 2.39): the domain NaN of `logf128`, `log2f128` and `log10f128` is the default negative one (unlike `logl`), and `log1pf128` returns a NaN operand quieted with its sign cleared (−qNaN and −sNaN both probed, M5-6). M5-6 probed the rest: the domain NaN of `asinf128` and `acosf128` is the default negative one (unlike `asinl`, `acosl`: positive), and `acosf128` keeps a NaN operand's sign (unlike `acosl`); `wide` selects the x87 forms by `F::EXPLICIT`. Every other NaN, flag and `errno` of the 14 names already matched glibc; `atanf128(±∞)` raises inexact with ±π/2 where glibc's `atanf128` raises none (kept: ±π/2 is rounded, so inexact is the flag of the correctly rounded result, and glibc's own `atanl(±∞)` raises it too). Known limit, the same as for `long double`: integral `pow` exponents whose exact result has more than about 350 significant bits rest on the 384-bit evaluation's margin, not on an exactness proof. |
| D-10.20 | §10.3 | — | **Special functions of `long double`** (milestone 5b). `math::special` is generic over `Float`: operands enter as their exact values (`mp::Mp`), so the 384-bit evaluation of D-10.15 serves `float`, `double` and x87 `long double` alike (`_Float128` next) and every result is correctly rounded in every mode. Format-dependent thresholds come from `Float::EMAX`/`PREC`: `erfc` underflows completely beyond `a² > (EMAX + PREC)·ln 2` (106.77 for `long double`), `tgamma` overflows when `lnΓ > (EMAX + 1)·ln 2 + 1` and underflows below `−(EMAX + PREC)·ln 2`, Bessel recurrences stop beyond `2^(EMAX + 100)`, `yn` takes the overflow shortcut beyond `(EMAX + PREC)·ln 2 + 50`. `sin(πx)` of the reflection splits `x` exactly in `Mp` (any significand up to 113 bits); Hankel's phase is reduced in 384 bits below 2^29 and by `mp::reduce_wide` above, so huge arguments up to the largest finite value are exact. `tgamma` is exact at the integers up to 92 (91! has 380 significant bits; was 60). Tiny `jn` arguments (below 2^-180, orders 1 to 91) whose leading term `(x/2)^n/n!` is a dyadic number (n = 1, 2, or the odd part of n! dividing odd(x)^n) are computed exactly and rounded just inside it (`jn_tiny`; the series drops the correction below 2^-392 and rounded such terms to the wrong side in the directed modes: found by the `long double` differential test, in code shared with `double`); orders of 92 and more underflow there; the `j1` shortcut moved from 2^-200 to 2^-180 into this rule. Recurrences of more than 5000 steps still run in double-double (relative error about n·2^-106, 2^-22 of a `long double` last place at n = 2^20: a known limit, as for `double`). Conventions as `float`/`double` (D-10.16), which the `long double` probe confirmed (`spec/behaviour/libm-special-ld.md`), except `lgammal(2)` downward: +0 as C F.10.5.3 requires (glibc −0; three-way, recorded). **`_Float128` (M5-7, 2026-10-22):** the same bodies (`s10_math.tsv` format `q`, 11 names; glibc has no `gammaf128`). Three thresholds that assumed at most 64-bit significands are derived per format: `erfc`'s beside-one shortcut below `2^min(−100, −PREC−36)` (−149), the switch from `1 − erf` to the continued fraction at 6 instead of 10 for `PREC > 64`, and every recurrence in 384 bits for `PREC > 64` (double-double's 106 bits are short of 113; cost O(n) 384-bit steps, a speed item for milestone 6). Precision bound per regime (bits of 384 left for a 113-bit result; correct rounding is claimed where about 2·113 + 10 = 236 remain, the usual estimate of the hardest case): `erf`, `erfc` of negative operands, `tgamma` (`\|lnΓ\| < 2^14`): over 360; `erfc` by `1 − erf` below 6: over 320 (at most 55 cancel); `lgamma` next to 1, 2 and its negative zeros: about 250 (results down to about 2^-114 against terms of 2^7); Bessel power series below about 20, Hankel above about 121, recurrences away from zeros: over 236. **M5-W (MATH-M5-MP-WIDE, 2026-10-22) closes the limit below by Ziv's strategy:** the power series and Hankel's expansion return an absolute error bound with each 384-bit value (the derivation is in `special.rs`: `5K²·2^emax·2^-383` for the series' `K` terms below `2^emax`, the first omitted term and the phase error for Hankel); `jn`/`yn` (so `j0`, `j1`, `y0`, `y1`) round only when both ends of that interval round to the same encoding and flags, and otherwise evaluate the power series again in 768 bits (`mpw`: the `mp` arithmetic expanded with twelve limbs by `mp::mp_core`, `π`, `ln 2`, `γ` from `cargo xtask tables`) for `x < 160` and orders up to 160 (no zero of `J_n`/`Y_n` lies below `x = n`). Next to a zero below 160 the 768-bit series keeps more than 380 bits (terms up to 2^226 at 160, results down to about 2^-130); Hankel at and above 160 keeps more than 330 of 384 (truncation 2^-461 at 160): both well above the 236 the hardest case is estimated to need. Every other operand decides in 384 bits and costs only the test (two roundings). Proof: `special_cr.rs` `float128_bessel_*_next_to_zeros` (the four `_Float128` operands around each zero of `J0`, `J1`, `Y0`, `Y1` on [20, 160) and of orders 2, 3 and 7, every mode, against the oracle with up to 2^16 bits); the generic code serves `float`, `double` and `long double` alike. The oracle's `euler_gamma` now scales its Brent–McMillan `n` with the precision (a fixed 96 was right to only about 550 bits). Still without a bound: the recurrences (orders above √x beyond 100, `n > 160` anywhere), which round their 384-bit value as before, and #841 (the `_Float128` recurrences run O(n) 384-bit steps up to 2^31, a speed item for milestone 6). **Former known limit (queued for M5-W, closed above):** the Bessel power series for 20 ≤ x < 100 next to a zero of `J`/`Y` (the terms reach e^x/√(2πx), about 2^140 at 100, against results down to 2^-117: about 120 bits left) and Hankel's expansion for 100 ≤ x < 121 next to a zero (truncation about e^(−2x) = 2^-288 at 100: about 170 left) are faithful, not proven correctly rounded; the ceiling of `libm-ulps.tsv` (`j0` 2, `j1` 4, `y0` 3, `y1` 5, `jn` 7, `yn` 5) holds with a wide margin. X87-NAN-RULE-AUDIT-2 (owner ruling 2026-10-23, #902): an invalid x87 encoding beside a number in `fmaxl`, `fminl`, `nextafterl`, `nexttowardl`, `powl` and `remquol` gives the default NaN with invalid; glibc's per-function results are listed in the differences row for those functions and registered as COMPAT-10 (not implemented). |
| D-10.21 | §10.5 | — | **Complex forwarders of `long double`, `_Float64x` and `_Float128`** (milestone 5, MATH-M5-CPLX-FWD). Rust cannot name `long double _Complex` (psABI class COMPLEX_X87: passed in memory, returned in `st(0)` real and `st(1)` imaginary) or `_Float128 _Complex` (32 bytes, memory both ways), so `cargo xtask math-gen` emits C forwarders into `csys/src/adapter/math_*.c` as for the real members (OD-C4, no assembly, #830): the C compiler handles the convention and converts through a union to `struct liella_ldc_bits`/`liella_f128c_bits` (two bit structs, real part first), which the Rust side receives and returns as `mathret::Complex<LdBits>`/`Complex<F128Bits>` (the `CPart` trait maps each part to its `liella-math` format). The exact members (`creal`, `cimag`, `conj`, `cproj`) are bit-identical to glibc, flags and `errno` included, on every encoding (x87 invalid encodings too); `cabs` is `hypot` and `carg` is the x87 `atan2` (`cargf128` waits for `atan2f128`), correctly rounded in every mode. `hypotl`/`atan2l` (and so `cabsl`/`cargl`) take their NaN by the x87 unit's rule as glibc does, through the general rule every x87 operation follows (`fused::nan_operands_by` with `Pick::X87`, X87-NAN-RULE-AUDIT: an invalid encoding gives the default NaN whatever the other operand, equal-significand NaNs of one kind give the positive one). Proof: `crates/math/tests/complex_ld_products.rs` (ABI sentinel with distinct parts, x87 tag word after 20 calls, the grid and random pairs in every mode against glibc and the oracle) and the member checks of `s10_math_symbols.rs`. X87-NAN-RULE-AUDIT-2 probed the rest black-box (`crates/math/tests/x87_nan_products.rs`, oracle `x87_nan_diff.c`, now with `cexpl` `clogl` `clog10l` `csqrtl` `cpowl` `cabsl` `cargl` on `a + bi`, NaN lines compared): `fmaxmagl`/`fminmagl` take the first of two quiet NaNs and the x87 rule once a signalling NaN or invalid encoding is present; `nexttowardl` is `nextafterl` (x87 rule on both operands); `powl` of a signalling NaN to −0 is its quiet NaN with invalid (+0 takes the same path, not probed); `fmodl`, `remainderl`, `dreml` (x, ±∞) and `scalbl` (x, ±0) return a pseudo-denormal x canonical (exponent 1); `cexpl(+∞ + i·invalid)` gives the default NaN; the other complex functions already matched. Liella follows each. KEPT difference (gain: a NaN for a non-number operand, as the x87 unit and every other Liella `long double` function give): an invalid encoding beside a number in `fmaxl` `fminl` `nextafterl` `nexttowardl` `powl` `remquol` gives the default NaN with invalid, where glibc returns the number, +0 or another invalid encoding (invalid raised on both sides); the test lists these pairs as KEPT. |
| D-10.22 | §10.3, §10.6 | — | **Hardware square root under the caller's control word** (M6-2, MATH-M6-SQRT and MATH-M6-SQRT-FTZ). `sqrt`/`sqrtf` run `sqrtsd`/`sqrtss` in place whenever every MXCSR exception is masked, in any rounding direction, with or without FTZ and DAZ (`fpu::is_sqrt_in_place`); `sqrtl` runs `fsqrt` at 64-bit precision control with every x87 exception masked; anything else (an unmasked exception) takes `fused::sqrt` on the operand as the caller's DAZ reads it. **Caller's FTZ/DAZ honoured (OWNER RULING 2026-10-23, MATH-M6-FPENV-HONOR; reverses the provisional calls #1278 (DAZ half) and #1490):** the caller's floating-point environment, FTZ and DAZ included, is the caller's choice and Liella does not subvert it. For every libm entry the envelope covers (`mathret::elem`, `lgamma`, `lgamma_r`, `sincos`, `cplx`, `cplx2`, `cplx_real`), for `sqrt`/`sqrtf`, and (MATH-M6-FPENV-HONOR-REST, #1509) for every software form whose result came through `mathret::ret` and its siblings, now `mathret::Soft` (`ret`, `ret_out`, `remquo`, `intmax`, `uintmax`: fma, fdim, the narrowing operations f32/f64 from wider formats, nextafter/nexttoward/nextup/nextdown, ldexp/scalbn/scalbln/scalb, ceil/floor/trunc/round/roundeven/rint/nearbyint, lrint/llrint/lround/llround, fromfp/ufromfp and the x variants, the fmax/fmin/fmaximum*/fminimum*/fmaxmag/fminmag families, fmod/remainder/drem/remquo, modf/frexp, ilogb/llogb/logb/significand, __iseqsig, hypot; `cargo xtask math-gen` emits the form when an operand or the result is `float`/`double`, and it enters the default word like the envelope so the internal arithmetic never runs under the caller's mode). Bit-level operations (`mret::pure` classification, `payload`, `canonical`, `cpart`) are not arithmetic and keep their operands. `long double` is x87: FTZ and DAZ are MXCSR (SSE) controls and do not apply to x87 arithmetic, so x87 operands keep their identities (a `daddl` or `faddl` operand is not read by DAZ, and their `double`/`float` result is not flushed by FTZ: black-box probe of glibc 2.39 under MXCSR FTZ, DAZ and both, MATH-M6-FPENV-HONOR-REST-2/-3, spec/behaviour/math-ftz-daz.md) and no rule is invented for them; `_Float128` is software and keeps its identities too: under the caller's DAZ a `float`/`double` operand that is subnormal is read as a zero of its sign (raising nothing); under the caller's FTZ a `float`/`double` result whose encoding is subnormal is a zero of its sign with underflow and inexact raised (the SSE unit's FTZ, Intel SDM), and so is a result of exactly the smallest normal that the computation reported as underflowed (tiny after rounding with an unbounded exponent, which the subnormal grid rounded up; probed on Haswell-EP host with mulss/mulsd under MXCSR FTZ in all four directions: zero, underflow+inexact; a value that the unbounded rounding takes to the smallest normal is not tiny and stays; test `ftz_flushes_the_tininess_edge`); `errno` stays what the computation reports. The internal arithmetic (double-double, error-free transforms, D-10.13) is NOT valid under FTZ/DAZ (a flushed error term would give a wrong result for normal operands), so it still runs in the default SSE word whenever the caller's differs, and the caller's DAZ/FTZ are applied at the boundary by the bits (`mathret::Denorm`): normal operands with normal results are bit-identical to the default word's. The hot path (caller's word already the default) tests only `in_place`. Not flushed: x87 `long double` (MXCSR does not reach the x87 unit) and `_Float128` (a software format). Known limits: the FTZ test is on the rounded result's encoding, so an exact value just below the smallest normal that rounds to it is not flushed (the hardware's tininess rule there not probed); the software forms follow the reference as probed (#1549, spec/behaviour/math-ftz-daz.md): fma, fdim, ldexp/scalbn and the narrowing from `float`/`double`/`_Float128` apply both DAZ and FTZ; the operand-returning forms are never FTZ-flushed (`Soft::kept`: fmax/fmin/fmaxmag/fminmag return the operand as DAZ reads it; `Soft::pick`: fmaximum*/fminimum* compare as DAZ reads and return the raw operand; `Soft::step`: nextafter gives `y` for operands equal as DAZ reads them, else steps the raw `x`; `Soft::raw`: nextup/nextdown/nexttoward step the raw `x`; a step from an `x` DAZ reads as zero raises nothing); fabs/copysign are bit operations; a form entered for the x87 unit (`Soft::enter(Unit::X87)`: daddl, faddl ... from `long double`) is never FTZ-flushed. sqrt follows directly: the hardware under the caller's DAZ gives +-0 for a +-subnormal, no flag, no EDOM, as glibc 2.39 does (black-box probe MATH-M6-SQRT-FTZ); there is no difference row for it. EDOM on the hardware path is set when a non-NaN operand gives NaN (exactly x < 0 as DAZ reads x). EDOM follows x < 0, never the sign bit (probe MATH-M6-SQRT-FTZ-2, glibc 2.39 Zen 1 host, identical under every FTZ/DAZ word and direction, all three formats): -0 gives -0 and a negative quiet NaN comes back unchanged, both with no flag and no EDOM; a negative signalling NaN comes back quieted with invalid and no EDOM; a negative normal operand (-1, -infinity, the smallest negative normal) gives the default quiet NaN, invalid and EDOM (probe MATH-M6-SQRT-FTZ-5, same words and directions, sqrt/sqrtf/sqrtl; x87 ignores FTZ/DAZ). Tests: `math_sqrt_hardware_matches_the_software_square_root`, `math_envelope_keeps_the_callers_mxcsr`. (Amended by D-10.101.) |
| D-10.23 | §10.11 | — | **cpow integer powers beyond the exact width** (MATH-M5-CPOW-EXACT, #1720). When the exact `z^n` (`0 < \|n\| <= 64`) does not fit the width of the current step and one part dominates the other by 2^6 or more, each part is the alternating, decreasing (negative-)binomial series of exact terms (`n < 0` only for a power-of-two dominant part); the exact partial sum and the sign of the first term below `2^(ex A − B)` decide the rounding in every mode at any width (`pow_int_far`, bound in its comment). Other inexact cases keep the ladder and, at 3072 bits, D-10.17's assumption. Tested: `cpow_integer_powers_beyond_the_exact_width` (float, double, long double, _Float128; 2^-16000 parts). |
| D-10.24 | §10.3 | — | **The real wide logarithms take a proven `ln`** (MATH-F128-WIDE-LN-PROVEN, #1939). The ten callers of the Halley `mp::ln` in `math::wide` and `math::special` now call `mp::ln_atanh` (the atanh series of D-10.17's kernels, absolute error `< 2^(max(e, 0) + 12 − B)` for `\|ln x\| < 2^e`, proved in its documentation; `B = 384`). Halley's form has no written bound (its convergence from a 1e-12 start is cubic, but its rounding errors were never bounded), so it is not used where a correctness claim rests on it; `mp::ln` stays only for the complex sites that still call it. The callers and what rests on them: `log`, `log2` (÷ `ln 2`), `log10` (÷ `ln_atanh(10)`) of `long double`, `_Float64x` and `_Float128` (D-10.19, correctly rounded): `\|ln x\| ≥ 2^-114` for `x ≠ 1` (`2^-65` for x87), so the result is within `2^-257` relative (x87 `2^-308`); `pow` (D-10.19): `z = y·ln\|x\|` within `\|y\|·2^(max(e,0)+12−384)`, and `\|y\| ≤ 2^(1−e)·\|z\|` with `\|z\| < 2^14` short of overflow, so `z` is within `2^-244` absolute and `e^z` within about that relative; `math::special` (D-10.20): Stirling's `ln y`, the shifted product's `ln`, the reflection's `ln π` and `ln\|sin πx\|`, `jn`/`yn`'s `ln(x/2)`, `ln(2/x)`, each within `2^-371` relative when `\|ln\| ≥ 1` and `2^-372` absolute below, inside D-10.20's per-regime budgets. Correct rounding still rests on an estimate, not a proof: the closest approach of `log`/`pow` of `_Float128` to a rounding boundary is not known; 257 (pow 244) bits exceed the `2·113 + 10 = 236` the estimate asks for. |
| D-10.25 | §10.2 | — | **FMA build of the `double` exp/log fast paths, chosen at run time** (MATH-F64-FMA-PATH; owner principle 2026-11-04: use all hardware options, never a different result; coordinator ruling #2261 widens UNSAFE(hot-kernel) to such calls). `fast64`'s `kernels!` macro builds `mul`, `mul_f64`, `reduce`, `exp_kernel` and `log_kernel` twice: with Dekker `two_prod` and, in `fast64::fused`, with `dd::two_prod_fma` (one `vfmsub`). Every product the kernels take is exact under either build (operands far from overflow, error terms representable), and an exact product's pair is unique, so both builds compute the same `y` and `eps`, take the same `None` branches and round the same: results are bit-identical by construction and each build has the error bounds proved at the kernels. `dispatch::FMA` (one byte set at startup like the AVX2 byte) is true only when CPUID reports FMA and the OS saves the AVX state, and `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.cpu.hwcaps=-FMA` clears it (the glibc tunable name; no new interface). `hot::exp_nearest`/`log_nearest` select the build; `selftest::set_math_fma` forces either for tests. Test: `crates/boundary/tests/math_fma_paths.rs` compares both builds bit for bit on a random sample. exp2, exp10, log2, log10 and pow remain single-path (plain build) until extended. |
| D-10.49 | §10.3 | — | **`float` Bessel fast path without a table of zeros** (LIBM-F32-BESSEL, coordinator ruling #2881). `j0f`, `j1f`, `y0f`, `y1f` evaluate in `double` (`fast32::bessel_core`): \|x\| in [2^-20, 2) a fit of J0, J1/x and of the regular parts R0, R1 with Y_n = (2/π) ln(x) J_n + R_n (− 2/(πx) for Y1); [2, 24) eleven pieces [c − 1, c + 1), one Remez fit in t = x − c each (degree 13 for J, 16 for Y: the log singularity at 0 slows the first piece); [24, 2^19) Hankel's form (DLMF 10.17.3) truncated after a_20/a_21. Each core returns an ABSOLUTE bound e and `bessel_finish` turns it into the per-call margin e·2^53/\|y\| ulp of y; near a zero the margin grows and the rounding test refuses, so the accurate path answers there and the results stay correctly rounded in all four modes with no table of zeros. Bounds: `bessel_bounds_hold` (Horner γ·Σ\|a_i\|r^i plus the Remez tool's measured fit error, Hankel's first neglected term < 2^-58 at 24) and `bessel_cores_are_within_their_bounds` (mp sums at ~1.3e5 operand/function pairs, worst error/bound 0.78). Fallback (round-to-nearest, a 2^16-point grid over (0, 64]): j0f 0, j1f 1, y0f 2, y1f 1 in 65536; on the exhaustive sweep (LIBM-F32-BESSEL-3: every encoding, all four modes, against the tiered oracle of ruling #2889 with its Bessel estimator `oracle32::bessel_est`) the fast path refuses 8784 of the 2617245696 calls in its range [2^-20, 2^19) for j0f (3.4e-6), 9928 for j1f (3.8e-6), 8936 of 1308622848 for y0f (6.8e-6) and 7228 for y1f (5.5e-6), the calls near the zeros; the accurate path answers those. The oracle needed its mp tier for 0 modes in all four sweeps. |
| D-10.50 | §10.2 | — | **The libm product decides its FMA builds itself, once, at load** (LIBM-F64-FAST-KERNELS-2 and -3, #2920, rulings #2965, owner failure-path-cost principle 10-21). `libm.a` and `libm.so.6` link their own copy of `liella-boundary`, everything but the math exports local, so the C library's startup (`cpu::init_with`) never writes libm's `dispatch::FMA` byte: before this row every program ran the baseline builds (cbench_libm counted the same with and without `-FMA`). libm's `.init_array` entry (`csys/src/adapter/libm_init.c`) calls `dispatch::liella_libm_start(argc, argv, envp)` once, which applies D-10.25's rule (`dispatch::fma_wanted`: CPUID FMA with the OS-saved AVX state, and `glibc.cpu.hwcaps` from the `GLIBC_TUNABLES` entry of `envp`; secure-execution mode, where `Tunables::parse` honours nothing, is asked only when that entry exists: `process::secure`, failing safe). It reads the `envp` argument, not the C library, because a dynamic program's loader runs libm.so.6's constructors before the C library's startup publishes the environment. A math call carries no is-it-decided test: one load and one test, as in the C library; code that runs before the constructor (a static program's constructors linked ahead of libm's) gets the baseline, which returns the same bits (D-10.25). The setting is the program's start-up environment, as for the C library's own choices. No new symbol in either library (`liella_libm_start` is local). Test: `crates/boundary/tests/libm_fma_select.rs` (user-mode instruction count of a static `-lm` program with and without `-FMA`). |
| D-10.51 | §10.2 | — | **Two-phase `double` elementary functions: a cheap quick phase with Ziv's rounding test in front of today's fast tier** (LIBM-RETHINK, LIBM-RETHINK-2; owner 2026-11-07 RETHINK direction; contract unchanged: D-10.3, D-10.13, D-10.17). Today's in-place tier (`fast64`, D-10.25) is an accurate phase on every call (bound 2^-70, two exact products, a degree-8 series, a serial Horner chain). The new tier 1 per family: Tang's table-driven reduction with a 128-entry table (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2) 1989), two-part Cody-Waite constants (Cody & Waite 1980), a short polynomial evaluated by Estrin's scheme (Estrin 1960; Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, 4.6.4), only the dominant product made exact where FMA is free, and a proven bound of about 2^-61.5 (SSE2, plain products) or 2^-67.4 (one FMA); Ziv's strategy (ACM TOMS 17(3) 1991) with the one-sided test of `fast64::near` (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007; CRlibm report 2006) and today's kernels, unchanged, as tier 2 (fallback 0.66% and 0.024% of the cbench operands). Average cost = quick + p·tier 2 (Muller et al., Handbook of Floating-Point Arithmetic, 2nd ed. 2018). Design targets per kernel: instructions, FP operations and the critical-path latency (the result is returned beside the test, not after it); verdict by timing. Measured on the prototype (`handoff/libm-rethink/proto/`, 0 mismatches with the CR exp over 9·10^8 checks): exp 135 -> 77 instructions (FMA builds; glibc 70); Ivy Bridge 40.8 -> 19.2 ns per call (glibc 13.8), latency 53.7 -> 33.6 ns (glibc 24.4); N100 27.0 -> 16.0 ns (glibc 8.0), latency 45.5 -> 31.3 ns (glibc 23.4): the N100 is bound by FP operations, so each kernel states its FP-operation count as a target. First family exp, exp2, exp10, expm1, then log, pow, sin/cos, atan. Both builds stay bit-identical (each correctly rounded). |
| D-10.52 | §10.3 | — | **Integer fixed-point quick tier for x87 `long double` and `_Float128` ahead of the 384-bit route** (LIBM-RETHINK, LIBM-RETHINK-2). Today every `long double` call outside exp/log and every `_Float128` call runs the 384-bit `mp` route (sinl 80 262 instructions, atanl 160 923, expf128 33 153; 95-99% in `mp`). The new tier 1 unpacks the operand to an integer significand and evaluates in 64-bit limbs: exact 64x64->128 products (`mul`; `mulx`/`adcx`/`adox` where BMI2/ADX exist), table-driven reduction and short fixed-point polynomials (fixed-point and multi-limb evaluation: Brent & Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010; Tang's tables; Payne-Hanek reduction for sin/cos/tan, Payne & Hanek, SIGNUM Newsletter 18(1) 1983), bound about 2^-85..-90 for x87 (2 limbs) and 2^-135..-150 for `_Float128` (3 limbs), Ziv's test as an integer mask test, the four rounding modes as four integer roundings (no MXCSR or x87 control-word traffic, so directed modes cost the same); tier 2 is `wide_dd` where it exists, then `mp`. Rejected: x87 transcendental instructions as the quick phase (their results are rounded to 64 bits, so the test would fail on about every call, and they are microcoded), triple-double in FP registers for `_Float128` (Lauter 2005: about 3x the operations of the 3-limb integer form). Estimates (to be measured by the first brief): expl 95-120 instructions, sinl 150-250 (glibc 1119), expf128 300-600 (glibc 6673). |
| D-10.53 | §10.5 | — | **Complex functions from the real quick phases with a per-part rounding test** (LIBM-RETHINK, LIBM-RETHINK-2). Today every finite complex operand off the axes runs the 384-bit route (`complex_body.rs`, generic over `Real`), so `cexpf` costs what `cexp` costs (116 554 and 116 569 instructions; glibc 162 and 239). The new tier 1 composes the real kernels' double-double results with their bounds: `cexp z = e^x (cos y + i sin y)` from one exp kernel and one shared sin/cos reduction, each part a product with relative bound ε_exp + ε_trig + the product's, one rounding test per part; `float` complex evaluated in `double` (bound about 2^-48). The formulas without cancellation stay those of the 384-bit route (clog near \|z\| = 1, csqrt from an accurate hypot, the inverse functions by Hull, Fairgrieve & Tang, ACM TOMS 23(3) 1997; branch cuts per Kahan 1987), as do the exactness detectors and special values; the 384-bit route stays the last tier. Estimates: cexp 180-250 instructions, cexpf 60-90, csqrt 60-90, clog 150-250. |
| D-10.54 | §10.2 | — | **`exp` quick phase: constants and bounds** (LIBM-F64-EXP-QUICK, under D-10.51; not wired, LIBM-F64-EXP-QUICK-WIRE wires it). `fast64::quick`: Tang N = 128 (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2) 1989), `ln2/128` in two parts with a 36-bit high part (Cody & Waite 1980), `k` from the shifted sum's bits, Taylor degree 6 by Estrin's scheme (Estrin 1960), Fast2Sum assembly (Muller et al. 2018), the one-sided test of `fast64::near` (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller 2007) with the result formed beside it; Ziv's strategy (Ziv 1991), `None` runs today's tier. Bounds proved in the module doc and recomputed by its tests: SSE2 2^-61.503 (stated 1.4375·2^-62), FMA 2^-67.727 (stated 1.25·2^-68); tables `EXP2_J128`, `LN2_128_CW`, `SCALE_128` from `cargo xtask tables`. Measured (LIBM-F64-EXP-QUICK-2, Haswell-EP): 0 mismatches over 10^8 operands per distribution and build (uniform [-10, 10], uniform bits over the domain, uniform [-745.2, 709.8]); fallback on uniform [-10, 10] SSE2 0.562%, FMA 0.0079%; largest relative error SSE2 2^-61.583; instructions per call with the fallback (not wired; targets 80 FMA, 95 SSE2): the count loop's results in handoff/LIBM-F64-EXP-QUICK.md. |
| D-10.55 | §10.5 | — | **`cexp`/`cexpf` quick tier, local details** (LIBM-CPLX-EXP-TIER, under D-10.53): `crates/math/src/complex_fast.rs`, `fast32/cexp.rs`. `double` for `2^-60 <= \|x\| <= 746`, `2^-30 <= \|y\| < 2^20` (the in-place entry in two builds, baseline and FMA as D-10.25, chosen at startup by `hot::cexp_nearest`, bit-identical and tested so; the any-mode envelope path stays baseline); part bound `(Ee·B + A·Et + 2^-99·A·B)(1 + 2^-48)`; `near` with `rho = 2^-62` then `fast64::settle`; a part is rounded unscaled and scaled by an exponent add only into biased exponents 2..2046, else the 384-bit route. `float`: `exp_core` × `trig_core` in `double`, margin 512 ulp, `fast32::round`. In-place nearest entry `mret::cplx_fast` (cold fallback restores MXCSR, then `cplx`). |
| D-10.56 | §10.3 | — | **x87 `sinl`/`cosl` integer tier: method and measurements** (LIBM-LD-TRIG-INT, LIBM-LD-TRIG-INT-2; D-10.52's first kernel; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). `crates/math/src/wide_int.rs`, called by `wide::sin`/`wide::cos` after the tiny-argument shortcut (`sincosl` calls both). (1) Reduction: Payne & Hanek (SIGNUM Newsletter 18(1), 1983) for every \|x\| >= 2^-34, one path: a 256-bit window of the generated `TWO_OVER_PI` table (it already covers x87 and binary128: no new table), three 64x64->128 products and one low product, truncation below 2^-190, the quadrant and the fraction f in [-1/2, 1/2). No Cody-Waite branch for moderate \|x\|: the window costs four products at every exponent (near 1e300 counts within 1% of [-10, 10]) and one path keeps one proof. (2) Tang's table method (Tang, ARITH 10, 1991): j = round(128\|f\|), 64 rows of sin and cos of jπ/256 in 128-bit fixed point (2 KiB), d = \|f\| − j/128 normalised (relative precision when j = 0). (3) Polynomials in u = d² with π/2 folded into the coefficients (no f·π/2 product): sine 5 terms, cosine 6, the inner Horner steps in 64-bit words, the last two in 128 bits (Brent & Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010, ch. 4). (4) Proved relative bound 2^-94 (the module documentation); the rounding test assumes 2^-92 (2^36 + 4 units of the 128-bit significand) and rounds in the four modes by integer tests, packing the x87 bits directly. Refusals take the 384-bit route: \|d\| < 2^-92 (never reached: the continued-fraction search of the x87 operands nearest the multiples of π/2, Muller, Elementary Functions, 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 11, finds \|f\| >= 2^-75) and what the test cannot decide (near a multiple of π/2 one of sin, cos is within 2^-92 of ±1 by design; the other is decided). Plain `mul` only: no `mulx`/`adcx`/`adox` variant written. Measured (saturation register section 25): 10^7 seeded operands in four exponent bands, 8x10^7 calls in four modes, 0 undecided, every result equal to the 384-bit route, worst error 2^-95.68; sinl 582 and cosl 583 instructions per call (glibc 1127; before this row 82 228), sincosl 1081 (glibc 1228); cycles per call on the Ivy Bridge timing host sinl 265 (glibc 548, 0.48x), sincosl 467 (glibc 630, 0.74x); the N100 figures are in the story report (handoff/reports/LIBM-LD-TRIG-INT-2.json). Open toward the brief's 300 instructions: sincosl's second reduction, the shared x87 entry (189 of 560 instructions), the kernel's variable 128-bit shifts. |
| D-10.57 | §10.0 | — | **Verdict cache of the math accuracy sweeps** (TVA-MATH-VERDICT-CACHE, owner ruling #3820). A sweep shard (the C-oracle sweeps complex_ld_cr, complex_f128, special_ld, special_f128, complex, elem_ld, special products; the pure-Rust special_cr and fast_gamma tests; the fast32 inverse-trig cores unit test) runs its D-10.3 check only when its input key differs from the key of its last green run; otherwise it prints `verdict cached: <name> <key>` and returns. Key (`crates/core/tests/support/verdict.rs`): the shard name; the test binary's bytes (`/proc/self/exe`, the image running: checker, mathtools oracle and every Liella byte a pure-Rust sweep calls); the `flags` line of `/proc/cpuinfo` (what the dispatch reads) and the kernel release; for C-oracle shards the shard index and count, the bytes of both programs (the static Liella program holds every Liella byte it runs; the reference program holds the C source's code) and of every shared object the reference program loads as the dynamic loader resolves them (`LD_TRACE_LOADED_OBJECTS`, ld.so(8): host libm, libc and loader); a sweep sized by an environment variable adds it (`LIELLA_GAMMA_SWEEP`). Complete because a shard's outcome is a function of exactly these: the programs run with an empty environment and read no files, the checker reads none, and what the code does beyond its bytes depends only on the CPU (dispatch) and the kernel (vDSO). Each file is hashed as two SipHash streams (128 bits) plus its length; an unreadable input makes the key incomplete (always run, never recorded). The record (`target/test-verdicts/<name>`, temporary file then rename, so per tree and host) is removed when a shard starts and written only by `pass()` after the last assertion, and only when the key read again then is unchanged, so a cached verdict is only ever a green one for identical inputs. `LIELLA_NO_VERDICT_CACHE=1` runs every shard (nightly and release runs). Tests: `crates/math/tests/verdict_cache.rs`. `verdict.rs` runs no program and touches no C code; the loader query (the only part that starts a program) is in `verdict_programs.rs`, included by the C-oracle sweeps only, so the pure-Rust special_cr stays `nextest::PASS0_ONLY`: that check lists the `#[path]` includes a pass-0-only target may have (`PASS0_INCLUDES`, `verdict.rs` only) and scans each with the target's own rules (TVA-MATH-VERDICT-CACHE-2; chosen over an exception that skips the include, which would leave its contents unchecked, and over dropping special_cr from the list, which would add a second run of a sweep the interposed exports cannot change, #889). |
| D-10.58 | §10.0 | — | **`remez --check` runs its fits in parallel and replays unchanged verdicts from a content-keyed cache** (GATE-REMEZ-CHECK-CACHE; D-10.12). Parallelism lives in the `remez` binary (`std::thread::scope`, at most `available_parallelism()` workers on a shared index; one process, one hash of the process image), each fit's output buffered and printed in command-line order, followed by that fit's `step: remez/<fit> <seconds>s` line (XTASK-TEST-STEP-TIMES; the fit's own time measured in its worker, a replayed verdict ~0.0 s, so the per-fit times overlap and no longer sum to the step's wall time), exit status the failure of any fit (a fit left unreported fails). With `--check`, each fit's key is SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4, std-only in `liella_mathtools::check_cache`: the workspace has no external crates and `std` has no 128-bit-or-wider hash) over tagged, length-prefixed fields: the running executable and every file mapped into the process (`current_exe` + `/proc/self/maps`: the executable, `ld-linux`, `libc.so.6`, `libgcc_s.so.1`), the mode, the fit argument and display path, the fit file, the `output` path and the coefficient file (absent is its own field). `strace -f -e trace=openat` of an uncached check over all 22 fits opened only those plus `/etc/ld.so.cache` (loader lookup), `/proc/self/cgroup` and `cgroup cpu.max` (worker count only; output order is fixed) and `/proc/sys/vm/overcommit_memory` (allocator). A fit that checks up to date stores its report in `<target>/remez-check/<key>` (temporary name + rename); a matching stamp prints the report and `up to date (cached <key>)` without fitting; a failing fit stores nothing; the generating mode never reads the cache; `LIELLA_REMEZ_NO_CACHE=1` turns it off. `tables --check` took 5.7 s: not cached. |
| D-10.60 | §10.2 | — | **`log` quick phase: method, table and bound** (LIBM-F64-LOG-QUICK, under D-10.51; wired as `log`'s tier 1, tier 2 = `fast64::log_nearest` unchanged, then the accurate path). `fast64::quick_log`: `x = 2^e·m`, `m` in `[45/64, 90/64)` read from the bits, 128 intervals (Tang, ACM TOMS 16(4) 1990); reciprocals `c_j` of 8 significant bits so `r = c_j·m − 1` is exact (Gal & Bachelis, ACM TOMS 17(1) 1991): SSE2 `c_j·(m − F_j) + b_j`, FMA one `fma`; `c_j = 1` on the two intervals next to 1; `−ln c_j` and `ln 2` with high parts on the `2^-42` grid so `e·Kh + Lh` is exact (`LOG_Q128`, `LN2_Q`, `cargo xtask tables`, 4 KiB). `log1p(r)` by Taylor degree 9 in Estrin's scheme (log's coefficients do not decay: degree 5-6 leaves `2^-45` next to 1; a rigorous minimax fit could save one term, not done), `r − r²/2` as an exact pair (2MultFMA, or a 26-bit split in SSE2), three Fast2Sums. Bound (module doc, recomputed by `log_quick_constants_and_bounds`): case `e = 0`, `c = 1` `2^-64.91`, case `e = 0`, `c != 1` `2^-67.63`, case `e != 0` `2^-70.9`; stated `RHO = 2^-64` both builds; Ziv one-sided test (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007) with `C = 0x3ff0040100401005`. Measured (Skylake-SP host): largest relative error SSE2 `2^-65.76`, FMA `2^-65.92` (3·10^5 / 10^5 operands vs `mp::ln`); fallback SSE2 797 of 800000 (0.0996%, model `C − 1 = 0.098%`), FMA 200 of 200000; every answer correctly rounded (2·10^6 SSE2, 2·10^5 per build through the entry). log2/log10/log1p not wired (follow-up stories). |
| D-10.61 | §10.3 | — | **`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `sincos` quick phase: one `π/64` reduction, today's table** (LIBM-F64-TRIG-QUICK, -2; under D-10.51; wired as tier 1 of the four entries, today's in-place tier is tier 2, the accurate path tier 3). `trig::quick`, SSE2 and FMA builds (D-10.50): `2^-26 <= \|x\| < 2^20` by Cody-Waite in three parts (Cody & Waite 1980) with `k` from the `1.5·2^52` shift (no conversion instruction); `\|x\| >= 2^20` by Payne-Hanek in integers (Payne & Hanek, SIGNUM Newsl. 18(1) 1983): three 64×64-bit products against a 192-bit window of `2/π`, declining when the fraction is below `2^-60`, nothing cached across calls (reentrancy); evaluation on today's 128-point `sin(jπ/64)` table (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2) 1989), Taylor `sin r − r` to `r^9` and `cos r − 1` to `r^8` by Estrin's scheme (Estrin 1960), only `C·r` exact, Fast2Sum assembly; `tan = sin/cos` with one division and its exact residual; Ziv's test (Ziv 1991; de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller 2007). Bound proved in the module doc and recomputed by its test: `RHO = 0.875·2^-61` (largest seen 2^-63.163), multiplier `1 + 2^-7 + 2^-12`; `tan` `2^-60` with today's `C_TAN`. **Why one `π/64` step, not `π/2` then `j/64`** (the brief's first method; coordinator accepted 11-07): the two-step reduction shrinks `\|r\|` to `2^-7` (one Taylor term less per series) but adds a second shift-and-subtract, an index, a quadrant select on the critical path and a second table; one step reuses today's table (no new cache lines) and has no quadrant logic (`cos` is index `n + 32`). Fallback on uniform [-10, 10]: SSE2 sin/cos 0.4-1.2%, tan 0.8-2.5%; FMA sin 0.83%, cos 0.81%, tan 1.62%. Tests: `trig/quick/tests.rs` (SSE2), `crates/boundary/tests/trig_quick.rs` (FMA, builds agree, ignored 10^8 accuracy job). Counts (cbench_libm instr/op, Skylake-SP, before -> after, glibc): FMA build sin 158.6 -> 131.7 (100.2), cos 156.4 -> 123.7 (104.7), tan 176.1 -> 157.9 (107.6), sin_huge 1345.1 -> 239.6 (365.8); SSE2 build after: sin 173.1 (122.3), cos 169.0 (126.1), tan 239.3 (124.2), sin_huge 291.7 (379.3); no other row moved by more than noise. Target sin <= 110 (FMA) not reached. Timing (cbench_libm time ratio vs glibc, before -> after, same host, interleaved): Ivy Bridge (SSE2 build) sin 2.22 -> 1.71, cos 2.13 -> 1.60, tan 2.83 -> 2.33, sin_huge 4.56 -> 0.71; N100 (FMA build) sin 2.13 -> 1.67, cos 1.83 -> 1.53, tan 2.64 -> 2.01, sin_huge 5.95 -> 0.87; no other row's instruction or cycle ratio moved. |
| D-10.62 | §10.2 | — | **`pow` quick phase: composition and run-time bound** (LIBM-F64-POW-QUICK, under D-10.51; wired as `pow`'s tier 1 behind `fast64::pow_domain`, which keeps every exact case out; tier 2 = `fast64::pow_nearest` unchanged, then the accurate path). `fast64::quick_pow`: D-10.60's log with one more Taylor term (degree 10) and its closing Fast2Sum, `ln x = lh + ll` within `KC·\|r\|³ + 2^-84·\|ln x\|`, `KC = 2.75u` (D-10.60's terms; `\|r\| <= 1.44·\|ln x\|` in every case); `y·lh` exact (2MultFMA, or Dekker's product with Veltkamp's split in SSE2: Dekker 1971), `tl = y·ll + e`; D-10.54's exp kernel on `th` with `tl` folded into the Cody-Waite step (`s = tl − kd·L2`, `rh + rl = r1 + s`), its bound recomputed for `\|rh\| <= (1 + 2^-32)·ln2/256` (stays within `RHO_FMA`, `RHO_SSE2`). Composed bound `rho = RHO_E + (KC'·\|y·r3\| + 2^-83·\|th\|)·(1 + 2^-38)`, and Ziv's test (Ziv 1991) with the one-sided test of de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller (2007) on a multiplier formed per call, `c = RN(\|y·r3\|·89/16 + C0)` (one FMA; `C0` from `RHO_E` with the `\|th\| < 708` part folded in), valid while `2^54·rho <= 2^-7`, which the domain `\|y·r3\| <= 2^-12`, `2^-60 <= \|th\| < 708` ensures. Module doc and `pow_quick_constants_and_bounds` (checked exactly at both ends of `\|y·r3\|`). Two builds, bit-identical where they answer. Measured (LIBM-F64-POW-QUICK-2, cbench_libm `pow`, Liella / glibc): instructions per call on the Zen 1 host 177.5 / 141.3 in the FMA build (before 319 / 143) and 247.7 / 191.5 with `--tunables glibc.cpu.hwcaps=-FMA` (before 494 / 193); time ratio 1.411 on Ivy Bridge (before 3.35) and 1.478 on the N100 (before 3.59), spread under 0.01, 5 rounds. |
| D-10.63 | §10.0, §10.2 | — | **One-pass `float` exp and exp2 in the caller's environment** (LIBM-F32-ONEPASS; DESIGN.md 3.1 A/B under D-10.51). `expf` and `exp2f` (and their `_Float32` names) no longer read MXCSR on the fast path: for 2^-26 ≤ \|x\| < 87.33 (exp) or 126 (exp2), tested on the bits before any floating-point operation, one `double` evaluation (Tang 1989 table of 2^(j/128) and a degree-4 Estrin polynomial, `fast32::exp_onepass`) runs in the caller's rounding direction, with a margin proved for every direction (ε ≤ 2^-43.71, test margin 1024 ulp of y), then one `cvtsd2ss` rounds in the caller's direction and raises inexact. Every intermediate is a normal `double`, so FTZ and DAZ (D-10.22) change nothing, and inexact is raised only for an inexact result (D-10.14: e^x is exact only at 0, which is refused, and 2^x at the integers, where the kernel is exact). Refusals (rounding test, range, NaN) go to the unchanged envelope; a NaN returns x + x before it. Proof by exhaustion: `math_expf_onepass_sweep`, `math_exp2f_onepass_sweep` (all 2^32 encodings x 4 directions, bits, errno and flags against the envelope); the sampled test also covers FTZ, DAZ and both. Literature: Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2) 1989; Muller et al., Handbook of Floating-Point Arithmetic, 2nd ed. 2018, ch. 10-11. Not yet converted: exp10f (an integer x up to 10 has an exact result that the multiply by 128·log2 10 makes inexact), the log family (log2 and log10 of exact powers), trig and powf. |
| D-10.64 | §10.2 | — | **`exp2` and `exp10` on the `exp` quick kernel** (LIBM-F64-EXP-FAMILY-QUICK, under D-10.51 and D-10.54). `fast64::quick::{exp2,exp10}_tiered` in both builds, wired in `hot/exp_log.rs`; tier 2 on a miss is today's `fast64::exp2_nearest` / `exp10_nearest` (which also answer exp2's integers exactly). The kernel from `T_j` on is exp's (one shared `kernel`); the reductions are their own: exp2 `k` from `RN(x·128 + 1.5·2^52)`, `s = x − k/128` exact, `r = s·ln2` with the product's low part exact by one FMA; exp10 `k` from `RN(128/log10 2)`, `log10(2)/128` in three Cody–Waite parts (`LOG10_2_64_CW` halved, exact), `r = (sh + sl)·ln10` (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2) 1989; Cody & Waite 1980). The SSE2 builds drop the product's low part (`<= 2^-62`) instead of a Dekker product: it doubles their bound (`RHO_FAM_SSE2 = 1.4375·2^-61`, fallback 1.14% instead of 0.57%), which at tier 2's cost is about one instruction per call against about six for the Dekker product on every call. FMA bound `RHO_FAM_FMA = 1.6875·2^-68` (fallback 0.010%). Exact cases: exp2 of an integer gives `zl = 0` exactly and is declined without raising inexact; exp10 of the integers 1..=23 is declined before the kernel (one compare on the hot path). Bounds recomputed from the constants by `quick/tests.rs::family_constants_and_bounds`. **`expm1`** (LIBM-F64-EXP-FAMILY-QUICK-2; Tang, "Table-driven implementation of the expm1 function", ACM TOMS 18(2) 1992: table region and polynomial region): `fast64::quick::expm1_tiered` in both builds, tier 2 today's `fast64::expm1_nearest`. `\|x\| >= 2^-5`: exp's reduction and kernel, then `vh − 1` by 2Sum and the kernel's low part added before one Fast2Sum, so the `−1` is folded in before rounding; the kernel keeps `th·rh`'s low part in the SSE2 build too (Dekker's product, about 13 more operations on this path only), because `e^x/\|e^x − 1\|` (up to 32.5 at `2^-5`) would magnify the dropped part to `2^-56.5` and a fallback rate near 18%. `\|x\| < 2^-5`: `x + x²/2 + x³·P(x)` (Taylor `1/3! ..= 1/9!`, Estrin) with an exact head: `xh` = `x` with its low 27 significand bits cleared (one AND), `x²/2 = xh²/2 + xl·(x + xh)/2`, the first product exact, so every bit of `x` reaches the result without a two-product. One stated bound for both builds and regions, `RHO_M1 = 1.5·2^-62` (computed `2^-62.57`/`2^-62.66` table region SSE2/FMA, `2^-62.04` series), expected fallback about 0.6%; the threshold `2^-5` balances the two regions' bounds. No exact cases (`e^x − 1` irrational for double `x != 0`). Bounds recomputed by `quick/tests.rs::expm1_constants_and_bounds`. |
| D-10.65 | §10.2 | — | **`asinh`/`acosh`/`atanh` (`double`) quick phase** (LIBM-F64-INVHYP-QUICK, under D-10.51; wired as the three entries' tier 1 through `elem_fast`, tier 2 = the accurate path `hyper` unchanged). `fast64::quick_invhyp`: the logarithm's argument as an unevaluated pair within `2^-98` (acosh below 2: `log1p(a + sqrt(2a + a²))`, `a = x − 1`; asinh below 1: `log1p(a + (sqrt(1 + a²) − 1))`; above: `ln(x + sqrt(x² ∓ 1))`; from `2^32`: `ln 2x`; atanh: `log1p(2a/(1 − a))/2` with one division and the remainder by an exact product), the root as `sqrtsd` plus one Newton correction, exact products by 2MultFMA or Dekker (Dekker 1971; Knuth TAOCP 2 4.2.2; identities as in Muller, Elementary Functions 3rd ed. 2016). New pair entries of D-10.60's kernel, `quick_log::log_pair_parts`/`log1p_pair_parts` (on the kernel's `split`/`join`, shared with D-10.66's `log1p`): the low part `d` folded in as `d·(1 − r + r²)`, stated `RHO_PAIR = 2^-63` (module docs derive each term), Ziv's one-sided test with `C_PAIR` (expected fallback 0.2%). Ranges `2^-200 <= \|x\| < 2^1000` (no spurious flag); outside them, and on a miss, `None`. Tests `crates/boundary/tests/invhyp_quick.rs` (both builds, correct rounding against the accurate path, fallback rate). Instruction counts and timing in handoff/LIBM-F64-INVHYP-QUICK.md. |
| D-10.66 | §10.2 | — | **`log2`, `log10`, `log1p` on the `log` quick phase** (LIBM-F64-LOG-FAMILY-WIRE, under D-10.51/D-10.60; tier 1 in both builds, tier 2 = today's `fast64::log{2,10,1p}_nearest` unchanged, then the accurate path). `log2`/`log10`: `log`'s unrounded `(zh, zl)` times `1/ln b` as one double-double product (FMA: 2MultFMA, error `< 2^-103`; SSE2: `zh` cut to 26 bits by a mask times a 26-bit `k26`, exact, plus two rounded cross terms, `< 2^-75.2`), then Fast2Sum; bound `log`'s worst case plus `2^-74` (`2^-64.9`), same `RHO = 2^-64` and `C`. A table pre-scaled by `1/ln b` was weighed and not taken: `r − r²/2` still needs a double-double product by `1/ln b`, so it saves no operation for `log10` and at most one for `log2`, for 4 KiB more table each. Exact results (`log2 2^k`, `log10 10^n`, `0 <= n <= 22`) are the only rational values and come out exact (`zh = RN(zh + zl)` within `RHO` of an integer); the product would raise inexact for them, which the in-place fast entry must not, so `log2_tiered` answers `2^e` with `e` from the bits and `log10_tiered` answers `10^n` (`1 <= n <= 22`) from a 71-entry table by binade, both before any arithmetic. `log1p`: `2^-60 <= \|x\| < 2^-8` by `log`'s series with `r = x` exactly (bound `2^-67`); `\|x\| >= 2^-8`, `−1 < x < 2^960`: `1 + x = yh + yl` (Fast2Sum, larger first), `log`'s reduction of `yh`, and `log1p(yl/yh) ≈ d·(1 + r² − r)` with `d = yl·c·2^-e` (`c·2^-e` from the bits; no division) added to the low sum: `2^-64.34` at worst; tiny `\|x\|` and `±0` stay with tier 2. Rounding test as D-10.60 (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007; Dekker 1971 for the products). Proofs in `fast64/quick_log.rs`'s module doc, recomputed by `log_family_constants_and_bounds`. Instructions per call (`bench --compare --counters`, cbench_libm, Zen 1 host), log2 / log10 / log1p: FMA build 111.4 / 111.2 / 113.3 (glibc 63.1 / 103.0 / 83.6; before this row, wl_percall: 195.2 / 205.4 / 245.0), SSE2 build (`glibc.cpu.hwcaps=-FMA`, both sides) 144.4 / 143.2 / 145.5 (glibc 83.2 / 118.4 / 103.1). |
| D-10.67 | §10.0, §10.2 | — | **One-pass `float` kernels take their operand into the `double` domain without a partial-register write** (LIBM-EXPF-RATCHET; amends D-10.63). `cvtss2sd` (like `cvtsi2sd`, `sqrtsd` and the other scalar SSE writes) replaces only the low lane of its destination and so depends on that register's previous writer; the compiler chose a register the function had not written, which held the previous call's result, so back-to-back `expf`/`exp2f` calls formed one latency chain (Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual: partial-register dependencies of scalar SSE). Rule: the one-pass entries build x·2^-896 from x's bits with integer operations (`fast32::onepass_scaled`; exact for every normal `float`, which the bit test guarantees) and move it in with a full-register `movq`; the 2^896 goes into the kernel's constant (exact, z = x·c normal, so the rounding in every direction and D-10.63's bound are unchanged). Cost +8 integer instructions per call (expf hot path 40 -> 48 instructions in libm.so.6); timing in the story report. A later one-pass kernel (exp10f, logf, trig) starts from `onepass_scaled` or checks its disassembly for a scalar SSE write into a register not written earlier in the function. (Amended by D-10.79.) |
| D-10.68 | §10.0 | — | **No libm export's hot path merges into an `xmm` register it has not written; `cargo xtask partial-write` checks it on the built `libm.so.6`** (LIBM-PARTIAL-WRITE-CHECK; follows D-10.67). Rule, from the Intel SDM vol. 2 instruction pages and the Intel Optimization Reference Manual (partial-register writes, dependency-breaking idioms), not from any library: the legacy-SSE forms whose low element is computed from the sources alone but which keep the rest of the destination (`cvtss2sd`, `cvtsd2ss`, `cvtsi2sd`/`cvtsi2ss` in every operand form, `cvtpi2ps`, `sqrtss`/`sqrtsd`, `rcpss`, `rsqrtss`, `roundss`/`roundsd`, register-to-register `movss`/`movsd`, `movlps`/`movlpd`/`movhps`/`movhpd` loads, `movhlps`, `movlhps`, `pinsrb`/`w`/`d`/`q`, `insertps`) carry a false dependency on the destination's previous writer; on a libm entry that writer is the previous call, so back-to-back calls become one latency chain (D-10.67 measured expf at 3.11x -> 1.66x the reference's time on the N100 class). Such an instruction passes when its destination is owned on that path: written earlier (any full write, including the `xorps`/`pxor` zero idioms the renamer resolves without waiting, `movq` from a GPR, memory-source `movss`/`movsd`), an argument register of the export (from its Rust signature; unknown types count all eight as arguments, which can hide but never invent a finding), or also a source of the instruction. The VEX forms merge from their first source (VEX.vvvv) instead and are checked on it. Scope: every path from each export's entry, both outcomes of every branch (so the FMA and SSE2 builds of one export), up to the first call, return or indirect jump, with joins intersected; a merge after a call is not reported. Wiring: `cargo xtask so` fails on a finding the allow-list does not name (after publishing, so the product can be read), `cargo xtask static` runs it when `target/liella/libm.so.6` exists and prints why it skipped otherwise. Findings on origin/next when it landed: 12 (`exp10f`, `logf`, `log2f`, `log10f` (a `cvtss2sd` and a `cvtsi2sd` each in the log family), `sinf`, `cosf`, `tanf`, `acoshf`, `asinhf`), allow-listed in `xtask/src/partial_write.rs` as a ratchet for LIBM-F32-ONEPASS-REST, which fixes and times them; a new finding fails the build. |
| D-10.69 | §10.3 | — | **`atan`/`asin`/`acos`/`atan2` (`double`) quick phase** (LIBM-F64-INVTRIG-QUICK, under D-10.51 and D-10.13). `invtrig::atan_quick` runs first on the reduced argument the fast tier already forms (`atan` below and above 1, `asin`'s and `acos`'s ratios, `atan2`'s quadrants), with the same rounding test (`EPS = 2^-62`); on a refusal today's kernel `atan_unit` runs on the same argument (tier 2, unchanged), then the accurate path. Method: Tang's table-driven reduction (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2), 1989; Muller, Elementary Functions 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 6) without a division: with `c = j/64`, `h = t − c`, `1 + c t = (1 + c²)(1 + g)`, `g = c h/(1 + c²)`, `\|g\| <= 2^-8`, so `v = h·R·(1 + s)` with `R = 1/(1 + c²)` from a new 1040-byte table `RECIP` (`rh` cut to 26 bits plus `rl`, within `2^-78`) and `s` the series of `1/(1 + g) − 1` to `g^7` as `−g + g²(1 − g)(1 + g² + g⁴)`; `h·rh` is an exact pair by one FMA or, in the SSE2 build, two masked partial products (no Veltkamp split); `atan v = v + v³P(v²)` as in the fast tier, on `RN(v.hi + vl)`. Bound `2^-63` relative (module comment derives each term; the reduction measured `2^-64.75` over 2·10^5 operands), so an answer is correctly rounded. Both builds compute the same pair `h·rh`, hence the same values. Tests `crates/math/tests/invtrig.rs` (the quick phase alone answers more than 98% and matches `mp::atan` at and around every node; the fast-tier tests cover the four entries in both builds). Counts and the continuation in handoff/LIBM-F64-INVTRIG-QUICK.md. |
| D-10.70 | §10.2 | — | **`cosh`/`sinh`/`tanh` (`double`) quick phase** (LIBM-F64-HYPERB-QUICK, under D-10.51; wired as the three entries' tier 1 through `elem_fast`, tier 2 = `fast64::hyperbolic` unchanged, then the accurate path). `fast64::quick` (module doc "cosh, sinh, tanh"): `e^a` and `e^-a` from ONE reduction of the exp quick kernel (Tang, ACM TOMS 15(2), 1989; `e^-a = 2^(-k/128)·e^(-r)`, the degree-6 Taylor polynomial split into even and odd parts so both sides share it); cosh `= (e^a + e^-a)/2`, sinh `= (e^a − e^-a)/2` for `2^-5 <= \|x\| < 23` (kernel low product kept: the cancellation multiplies its error by `coth 2^-5 = 32`), Taylor's odd series `1/3! ..= 1/9!` below `2^-5`, `e^a/2` from 23 to 708; tanh `= N/(N + 2)` with `N = expm1(2\|x\|)` from the expm1 quick pair (Tang, ACM TOMS 18(2), 1992), one division plus a residual correction (Dekker 1971). Every composition is bounded below `RHO_M1 = 1.5·2^-62` and decided by Ziv's one-sided test with `C_M1` (Ziv, ACM TOMS 17(3), 1991; de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007). Domains `2^-60 <= \|x\| < 708` (cosh, sinh) and `<= 22` (tanh): outside them, overflow thresholds, tanh's saturation and flags stay tier 2's and the accurate path's. The sinh series is Taylor's, not minimax (a minimax odd polynomial could drop a term: not tried). Tests `crates/boundary/tests/hyperb_quick.rs` (clause s10_0_f_0). |
| D-10.71 | §10.3 | — | **`sqrt`, `sqrtf`, `sqrtl` entries: nothing on the in-place path but the mode test and the instruction** (LIBM-SQRT-ENTRY). `sqrt`/`sqrtf` read MXCSR inline (`fpregs::mxcsr`, D-X.44), test `fpu::is_sqrt_in_place` as before, pin the operand behind the test and issue `sqrtsd`/`sqrtss` inline (`hot::sqrtsd`/`hot::sqrtss`, upper lanes `+0`: exact in every mode), with the EDOM store out of line (`sqrt_domain`, cold): the two calls (`liella_machine_mxcsr_get`, `liella_machine_sqrtsd`/`sqrtss`) are gone. `sqrtl`/`sqrtf64x` are assembly (csys/src/machine/sqrtl.S): `fnstcw`, the default-but-rounding test, `fldt` from the caller's stack slot, `fxam`, and `fsqrt` in place for a positive normal operand only; every other control word or class (zeros, subnormals, pseudo-denormals, infinities, NaNs, negatives, unsupported encodings) tail-calls the generated forwarder, now hidden as `liella_slow_sqrtl` (math-gen `ASM_ENTRY`), whose rules (D-10.20, D-10.22) are unchanged. Why: the generic forwarder rebuilt the 80-bit operand from two integer stores before each `fldt` (once in the C forwarder, once before `liella_machine_fsqrt`), and a load spanning two stores is not store-forwarded (Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual, store forwarding restrictions): a stall per crossing at equal instruction counts. The mode test stays: an unmasked exception must not see the instruction trap where the software path answers (D-10.22). Behaviour unchanged. (Amended by D-10.101.) |
| D-10.72 | §10.0, §10.2 | — | **`exp10f`, `logf`, `log2f`, `log10f` on the one-pass `float` path** (LIBM-F32-ONEPASS-REST; extends D-10.63 under D-10.67 and D-10.68). `exp10f` runs `fast32::exp_onepass` with c = RN(128·log2 10) for \|x\| < 37.9 (\|z\| < 2^13.98, the bound of D-10.63 unchanged); 10^n is a `float` for n = 1..=10 while z is inexact there, so operands in [1, 10] with their low 20 bits clear are refused on the bits before any arithmetic (two instructions on the hot path).
