The log family (`fast32::log_onepass`) splits a positive normal x = 2^e·m (m in [0.75, 1.5)) on the bits and builds m and e as `double`s by integer operations and a full-register `movq` (e via the 1.5·2^52 shift, exact), with the `log_core` table kernel (LOG_INV/LOG_C, degree-6 Estrin); `log2f` adds e + t·(1/ln 2) so x = 2^n stays exact with no flag, `log10f` refuses x = 10^n (n = 1..=10) by one load from a 32-entry table indexed by the exponent mod 32 (the ten exponents differ mod 32). Bound in every direction ≤ 2^-44.7 (< 313 ulp, test margin LOG_DELTA 640); the proof is the doc comment of `log_onepass`, checked by the exhaustive tests (2^32 operands × 4 directions against the envelope, 0 mismatches for each of the four). No exception table: the margin test is direction-independent. Removes the seven `partial-write` ALLOW entries of these four functions. Counts and timing in handoff/libm-f32-onepass-rest.md. LIBM-F32-ONEPASS-REST-3: `sinf`, `cosf`, `tanf` (`fast32::trig_core`, so also `sincosf` and the `float` complex and Bessel paths that share it), `asinhf` and `acoshf` test their fast range on the bits (one subtract and unsigned compare: 2^-26 ≤ \|x\| < 2^19 for trig, 2^-26 ≤ \|x\| < ∞ for asinh, 1 < x < ∞ for acosh) and build the `double` operand from them: a normal `float` with biased exponent e and fraction f is the `double` with exponent e + 896 and fraction f·2^29, sign copied, which is exactly the conversion. The values and the refusal sets are unchanged, so the existing proofs hold; the exhaustive sweeps (2^32 operands × 4 directions) re-check each function. Removes the last five `partial-write` ALLOW entries (the list is empty). |
| D-10.73 | §10.3 | — | **x87 `expl`/`exp2l`/`exp10l`/`expm1l` and `logl`/`log2l`/`log10l`/`log1pl` integer tier: method and proof** (LIBM-LD-EXPLOG-INT, LIBM-LD-EXPLOG-INT-2; D-10.52's second kernel family; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). `crates/math/src/wide_int_el.rs` is the first tier of the eight functions for the format with a 64-bit significand, ahead of the double-double tier (`wide::tiers`); the x87 entry and the integer rounding test of `wide_int` (D-10.56) are shared, not duplicated. Exponentials: Tang's table method (P. T. P. Tang, "Table-driven implementation of the exponential function in IEEE floating-point arithmetic", ACM TOMS 15(2), 1989) in 64-bit limbs: `x·128/ln2` exact in 192 bits, `k = round`, `r = f·ln2/128` (magnitude below `2^-8.5`), `e^r − 1` by a degree-10 fixed-point Horner, a 128-entry `2^(j/128)` table; `expm1` uses the exact `x` when `k = 0`. Logarithms: Tang's logarithm table method (ACM TOMS 16(4), 1990) with a two-step multiplicative reduction (W. F. Wong, E. Goto, IEEE TC 43(3), 1994): 128 entries of 17-bit reciprocals, then 65 entries around 1 (second reduced argument below `2^-12.98` in magnitude), a degree-8 series; `log2`/`log10` by one product; `log1p` feeds the exact `x` below `2^-7`. Horner in fixed point per Brent and Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic (2010), ch. 4. Proved bounds (module documentation, steps E1-E4 and L1-L4): exponentials `2^-110.4`, `expm1` `2^-101.8`, logarithms `2^-103.2`; the rounding test assumes `2^-92`. Measured: 10^7 random operands per function in four modes, exponentials 0 undecided, worst `2^-112.0` (`expm1` `2^-103.6`); `logl` worst `2^-103.9` with 0.064% of calls undecided (they go on to the double-double tier; cause open, LIBM-LD-EXPLOG-INT-3). Results outside the normal range and the operands the entry points settle first (`expm1` below `−50.8`, `log 1`) are refused and go to the later tiers. Reuse: `exp_fix`, `exp_table` (powl passes its own `k` and the magnitude of `r`), `ln_fix` (any positive `t·2^q`). Not adopted: x87 `f2xm1`/`fyl2x` as the quick phase (faithful at best, microcoded), tuning the double-double tier in place, triple-double (DESIGN section 21). Tests: `wide_int_el::tests::{constants_are_the_rounded_values, tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route, hairline_results_are_refused, tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route_long}`. Timing (Ivy Bridge, N100) and instruction counts: not yet measured (LIBM-LD-EXPLOG-INT-3). |
| D-10.74 | §10.5 | — | **`clog`, `csqrt`, `clogf`, `csqrtf` get a quick tier in front of the 384-bit route** (LIBM-CPLX-LOG-SQRT, under D-10.53; every decline reaches the route unchanged, so special values and the Annex G cases stay as they were). `double`, window `2^-400 <= \|x\|, \|y\| < 2^400` (no scaling step; outside it the route). `csqrt` in Kahan's form (Kahan, "Branch Cuts for Complex Elementary Functions, or Much Ado About Nothing's Sign Bit", 1987): `t = sqrt((\|x\| + \|z\|)/2)` from a double-double `\|z\|` (Dekker 1971 products, the correctly rounded `sqrt` plus one Newton correction), the other part `\|y\|/(2t)`; no subtraction, so both parts are within `2^-101.9` relative (test bound `2^-100`); the signs follow the cut (`x < 0` swaps the parts, the imaginary part takes `y`'s sign). A part whose double-double is exact (`\|P.lo\| <= eps`) declines, so exact roots and their flags come from the route; a midpoint is impossible for a square root's part. `clog`: imaginary part from `atan2`'s quick phase (`atan2_abs`, split out of `atan2_nearest` before its rounding test, `2^-65.5` relative, ratio window `min/max >= 2^-60`); real part `log(a²+b²)/2` from the `log` quick kernel when `RN(a²+b²)` lies outside `[0.75, 1.25)`, else `log1p(w)/2` with `w = (a−1)(a+1) + b²` built from exact products, bound `2^-63·\|z\| + 2^-102·(\|(a−1)(a+1)\| + b²)`, so deep cancellation near `\|z\| = 1` shows in the bound and declines. One rounding test per part (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007), all four modes. `float`: the same formulas in plain `double` (`csqrtf` within 16 ulp of `double`, `clogf` 32 ulp per part) with `float`'s rounding test on the `double` result. The boundary's in-place nearest entries use `sqrtsd`; the envelope's modes use the software root, identical by construction. Tests: `complex_fast_ls_tests.rs` (each tier against the route in four modes, regimes near `\|z\| = 1` and the axes, exact roots, branch-cut sides, a 10^7 sweep). AXES (LIBM-CPLX-LOG-SQRT-4): an operand with an exact-zero part, which the general tier declines, is answered out of line in the in-place entries before the route (C Annex G.6.3.1, G.6.3.2, G.6.4.2 fix the zero part's sign): `csqrt(x±0i)` = `(√x, ±0)` for `x > 0` and `(+0, ±√\|x\|)` for `x < 0` (one hardware root, correctly rounded); `csqrt(±0+iy)` = `(t, ±t)` with `t = √(\|y\|/2)` (the halving is exact inside the window); `clog(x±0i)` = `(log\|x\|, ±0 or ±π)` from the correctly rounded `log` quick phase, `clog(±0+iy)` = `(log\|y\|, ±π/2)`, `clog(1±0i)` exact, any other unit-modulus axis operand declines; `cexp(x±0i)` = `(exp x, ±0)`, `cexp(±0±0i)` = `(1, ±0)`. `clogf` uses `clog`'s formula with `b = 0` (`a²` and `(a−1)(a+1)` exact in `double`); `csqrtf` takes the `double` root of the widened operand and rounds once to `float`, which is correctly rounded because `53 >= 2·24 + 2` (Figueroa, "When is double rounding innocuous?", SIGNUM 1995). Not covered (still the route): the `cexpf` axes, `cexp(±0+iy)`, zero and subnormal parts. Test: `complex_axes_in_place_match_the_route` (bits, flags and errno of the exported functions against the 384-bit route on both axes, signed zeros, six functions). |
| D-10.75 | §10.3 | — | **x87 `atanl`/`atan2l`/`asinl`/`acosl`/`tanl` integer tier: method and proof** (LIBM-LD-TRIG-INVERSE-INT, LIBM-LD-TRIG-INVERSE-INT-2; D-10.52's third kernel family after D-10.56 and D-10.73; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). `crates/math/src/wide_int/arc.rs` is the first tier of the five functions for the format with a 64-bit significand, ahead of the 384-bit route of `wide`; the reduction, the `sin`/`cos` polynomials and the integer rounding test of `wide_int` (D-10.56) are shared, not duplicated. One arc kernel `A(y, x) = atan(y/x)` for `0 < y <= x`: Tang's table method (P. T. P. Tang, "Table-lookup algorithms for elementary functions and their error analysis", ARITH 10, 1991) with `c = j/128` (128 entries `atan(j/128)`, 2 KiB), `r = (y − cx)/(x + cy)` formed exactly on operands truncated to `2^-120`, `atan r = r·P(r²)` with 7 odd terms by fixed-point Horner (R. Brent, P. Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010, ch. 4; three steps in 64-bit words, three in 128 bits). Quotient and square root: a `double` estimate (one `divsd`) refined by one exact integer residual, Newton's correction (Brent and Zimmermann ch. 3; J.-M. Muller, Elementary Functions, 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 2); no integer `div`; the root's seed is a `double` root within `2^-52` that the caller passes: the boundary's `sqrtsd` for `asinl`/`acosl` (the math crate forbids `unsafe` and cannot issue it; `wide::asin_sqrt`, `wide::acos_sqrt`), a truncated integer root (`soft_sqrt`) for the crate's own callers. Measured with the integer root `u128::isqrt` as the seed: `asinl` 1189 and `acosl` 1237 instructions per call against `atan2l` 869, the root about 330 of them. Compositions: `atan x = A(\|x\|, 1)` or `π/2 − A(1, \|x\|)`; `atan2` the same on `(\|y\|, \|x\|)`, then `π − θ` for `x < 0`; `asin a = atan2(\|a\|, s)`, `acos a = atan2(s, \|a\|)` (`π −` that for `a < 0`) with `s = √(1 − a²)`, `1 − a²` exact for `\|a\| >= 1/2`; `tan` takes the `sinl`/`cosl` reduction and polynomials once and divides `sin\|a\|` by `cos\|a\|` (the other way round in odd quadrants). Proved bounds (module documentation, steps 1-6): quotient `2^-101.8`, root `2^-101.4`, `atan`/`atan2` `2^-100.6`, `asin`/`acos` `2^-100.1`, `tan` `2^-94.1`; the rounding test assumes `2^-92`, and what it cannot decide goes on to the 384-bit route. Operands the entry points settle first (`atan2` with `x > 0` and `\|y/x\| < 2^-72`, the cubic-tiny ranges, `\|a\| >= 1` for `asin`/`acos`) never reach the tier. Constants from Python `decimal` at 200 digits, pinned against the 384-bit arithmetic. Not adopted: x87 `fpatan`/`fptan` as the approximation (no published error bound to build the rounding test on). Tests: `wide_int::arc::tests::{arc_constants_are_the_rounded_values, quotient_and_root_meet_their_bounds, arc_tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route, arc_tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route_long}`. Measured: 10^7 operands per function in four modes (half in each function's hard region) against the 384-bit route, 0 mismatches, undecided 0 (`atanl`, `atan2l`, `tanl`), 4 (`asinl`) and 8 (`acosl`) of 4·10^7 calls, worst `2^-103.4` (arcs) and `2^-96.85` (`tanl`); unit sweep root `2^-103.7`, quotient `2^-103.5`. Instructions per call (Skylake-SP class host; before this tier, after, reference): `asinl` 175971, 1029, 109; `acosl` 178209, 1066, 49; `atan2l` 167574, 869, 53; `atanl` 161286, 657, 26; `tanl` 89263, 769, 1080. x87 rows are judged by timing in cycles, not instructions; timing not yet measured. |
| D-10.76 | §10.3 | — | **`jn`, `yn`, `jnf`, `ynf` (orders `\|n\| >= 2`) take a recurrence tier before the 384-bit path (LIBM-F64-BESSEL-N).** `crates/math/src/fast_bessel_n.rs` builds a double-double value with a proved absolute bound from the fast `J0`, `J1`, `Y0`, `Y1` kernels (D-10.13's fast tier) and settles it with a rounding test in the caller's mode; a bound that does not settle, and every operand or result outside the tier's range, goes to the 384-bit path unchanged, so results stay correctly rounded (D-10.13). Method: `yn` by the forward three-term recurrence (A&S 9.1.27, stable upward); `jn` by the power series when `x² <= n + 1` (A&S 9.1.10), the forward recurrence when `n <= x`, and otherwise Miller's backward recurrence normalised by the forward value at `⌊x⌋` (Gautschi, SIAM Review 9 (1967); the start index from the ratio bound `J_k/J_{k−1} <= x/(2k − x)`); the `float` forms through the same `double` kernels with a `float` rounding test. Error bounds: a rounding error at step `k` reaches index `m` through the Casoratian `(πx/2)(Y_k J_m − J_k Y_m)` (A&S 9.1.16), bounded with `\|J_k\| <= min(1, (x/2)^k/k!)` (A&S 9.1.60, 9.1.62) and the modulus `M_ν = (J_ν² + Y_ν²)^(1/2)`, increasing in `ν` (Nicholson's integral, DLMF 10.9.30); on the oscillatory side by Cauchy-Schwarz `\|Y_k J_m − J_k Y_m\| <= M_m²` with `M_m` bounded from both recurrences (the smaller root of `M <= a + cM²`, capped a priori by the first bound); double-double step errors per Joldes, Muller and Popescu, ACM TOMS 44 (2017). Declines by design: orders above 4096, `\|x\|` outside `[2^-990, 2^500]`, forward values beyond `2^960` (`yn`'s overflow region), and the oscillatory side above about `x = 2^100` where the a priori cap fails. Tests: `crates/math/tests/fast_bessel_n.rs` (the tier against the 384-bit path in four modes per regime with a settled share of at least 95%, operands next to zeros, kernel bounds against the 240-bit oracle, rounding-test straddles, and an ignored 10^7-operand sweep per function). |
| D-10.77 | §10.3 | — | **`exp`'s quick rounding test has no `w != 0` guard** (LIBM-F64-QUICK-PROFILE; amends D-10.51's test for `exp` only). `exp_quick` and `exp_tiered` accept `zh` when `zh + zl·c == zh`, the one-sided test of de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller (RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007) with the unchanged `c` (`C_SSE2`, `C_FMA`). Bound: when the test passes with `zl = 0`, the error of `zh` is at most `rho·zh < 2^-61·zh` in magnitude (`RHO_SSE2 = 2^-61.476`, `RHO_FMA = 2^-67.678`), below a quarter of `ulp(zh)` and so below half the gap on either side of `zh` (the narrower gap below a power of two included), and `e^x` is neither a double nor a midpoint for a double `x != 0` (Lindemann–Weierstrass): `zh` is `e^x` rounded to nearest. The guard is kept where exact results exist (`exp2` at integers, `exp10`'s declined integers, D-10.64) and in the hyperbolics and `expm1`. Measured (Zen 1, wl_percall, cbench_libm's `[-10, 10]` operands): FMA build 91 -> 88 instructions per call, SSE2 build 104.2 -> 102.2 (glibc 69 / 79); log, log2, log1p, pow, sin unchanged. Measured and not kept: evaluating the kernel's `tl·(1 + rh)` as `tl·rh + tl` (one FMA in the FMA build) left the FMA build at 88 and made the SSE2 build 103.2 (+1). Plants: the test shortened to `c = 1` misrounds a hard case through `exp_quick` and through the entry (both caught). |
| D-10.79 | §10.0, §10.2 | — | **`sinf`, `cosf`, `tanf` (and their `f32` names) take their `double` operand from one in-place `cvtss2sd`** (LIBM-SINF-IVB-RATCHET-2, coordinator ruling #4434; amends D-10.67). The boundary wrappers `hot::f32_trig::{sinf,cosf,tanf}_nearest` pass `hot::fpregs::widen` (inline `cvtss2sd xmm0, xmm0` with `in("xmm0")`/`lateout("xmm0")`, destination = source, `%xmm0` being where the psABI passes the `float` argument; `inout` refuses operands of two sizes; category *machine-register*, its third template by coordinator ruling #4445, `nomem`, not `pure` so it stays behind the range test) into `fast32::{sin,cos,tan}_nearest_widen`, which run `trig_core_with`: the same core as `trig_core`, whose operand D-10.72 builds from x's bits in six integer instructions. The conversion runs only on a normal `float` with biased exponent 101..=145 (the range test refuses NaN, ∞, subnormals and zeros on the bits first), where it is exact and raises nothing, so results and flags are unchanged. Why: the Ivy Bridge `sinf` loop is throughput-bound (IPC ~2, reservation station full 46% of cycles, LIBM-SINF-IVB-RATCHET), so the bit-built operand's +6 instructions per call cost `sinf` 3.5% there; a `cvtss2sd` whose destination is its source merges only the operand's own register (no false dependency, D-10.67), in one instruction. LLVM ties the destination of a plain `f64::from(x)` only when x is dead afterwards, and x stays live for the refusal paths, so the tie needs the asm. The partial-write check (D-10.68) accepts the in-place form and still reports a conversion into another unowned register (tests `in_place_conversion_passes_and_another_destination_does_not`); `cargo xtask static` permits the template `cvtss2sd xmm0, xmm0` in `hot/fpregs.rs` only, `nomem` on exactly `in("xmm0")` and `lateout("xmm0")`, and no other machine-register invocation names a register (`machine_register_tests`). `sincosf`, `cexpf` and the Bessel cores keep the bit-built operand. Measured (LIBM-SINF-IVB-RATCHET-3): sinf and cosf 85.1 instructions per call (91.2 with the bit-built operand); interleaved Liella/glibc time ratios, median of 6 rounds, this change against the same tree with the bit-built entries: Ivy Bridge sinf 1.70 (1.83), cosf 1.69 (1.81), tanf 0.79 (0.82), asinhf 1.33 (1.41), acoshf 1.43 (1.43); N100 sinf 1.86 (2.33), cosf 1.74 (2.18), tanf 0.56 (0.68), asinhf and acoshf unchanged; expf control unchanged on both. |
| D-10.82 | §10.0, §10.2 | — | **`asinf`, `acosf`, `atanf` and `atan2f` on the one-pass `float` path** (LIBM-F32-REST; extends D-10.63 under D-10.67 and D-10.72). Each entry tests its fast range on the bits (asinf and atanf 2^-26 ≤ \|x\| < 1 or < ∞, acosf normal \|x\| < 1, atan2f both operands normal and finite), builds the `double` operands from the bits (exponent rebased by 896, fraction moved up 29 places: no `cvtss2sd`), evaluates once in `double` in the caller's MXCSR without reading it, applies the sign before the conversion, refuses when the result's low 28 significand bits lie within 64 of a rounding boundary (one add, mask and compare, the same in every direction), and converts once with `cvtsd2ss` in the caller's direction (`mathret::elem32_onepass`, and `elem32_onepass2` for atan2f). The square root of asinf and acosf is the boundary's `sqrtsd` (correctly rounded in the caller's direction). The shared reduction `fast32::atan_red_any` is the table method of the existing kernel (atan s = atan(i/32) + atan((s - c)/(1 + s·c)), odd degree-7 fit; Muller, Elementary Functions, 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 6, table-based reduction) with an index that does not depend on the direction: s·32 is rounded to the 2^-7 grid by adding 1.5·2^45 and the nearest integer is taken on the bits, so \|s - c\| ≤ 1/64 + 2^-12 in every direction (a round-to-nearest `s·32 + 1.5·2^52` gives the floor or the ceiling under a directed mode, outside the fit's interval), and c = i/32 is rebuilt from i through the 1.5·2^52 shift (no `cvtsi2sd`). Bound in every direction ≤ 21u (u = 2^-53; the proof is the doc comment of `atan_red_any` and its callers), margin 64 ≥ 1.5·24 + 1. Every result in the fast range is irrational (Niven; Lambert: tan and sin of a nonzero rational are irrational), so the conversion raises inexact and nothing else; atan2f refuses results below 2^-126 so it never underflows. Proof by exhaustion for the one-argument functions (all 2^32 operands × 4 directions against the envelope, 0 mismatches each); atan2f by the bound and a 10^9-pair job (4 directions) against the envelope. Counts and timing in handoff/LIBM-F32-REST.md. |
| D-10.84 | §10.3 | — | **`erf`/`erfc` (`double`) quick phase** (LIBM-F64-SPECIAL-QUICK, under D-10.51 and D-10.13): the C entries' in-place path (`hot::erf_nearest`, `hot::erfc_nearest`) runs a quick phase inside `fast_special::erf_nearest` / `erfc_nearest`'s own `\|x\| >= 2^-5` table branch (one range check shared with the table path, so the series path and `erfc` above 1 see no added compare; LIBM-F64-SPECIAL-QUICK-2), then the unchanged table path, then the accurate path. Quick domain: `erf` on `2^-5 <= \|x\| < 6`, `erfc` on `(−6, 1)` with `\|x\| >= 2^-5`. Method: the existing `ERF_T` Taylor rows (no new table) evaluated to degree 12 instead of 14 with one exact product in place of four double-double steps; the polynomial split by Estrin's scheme (Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, 4.6.4) into three independent Horner chains joined by `t⁴`, so the critical path is about half the degree-12 Horner chain; `P0 + P1·t` exact by one product and Fast2Sum (Dekker 1971), the low parts summed before `t²·r`. Bound: `RHO_ERF_Q = 2^-62` relative (largest slot 2^-62.017) (erf, erfc below 0) and `RHO_ERFC_Q_LOW = 2^-61` (2^-61.55) (erfc on `(0, 1)`, `1 − erf`'s absolute error over `erfc`'s least value per slot), proved per slot by the generator's `quick_bound` (truncation by Cramér's inequality, Abramowitz and Stegun 22.14.17; every operation counted as a rounding, valid for both builds) and asserted by `special_tables::quick_tests`. Rounding: the one-sided constant test `fast64::near` (de Dinechin, Lauter & Muller, RAIRO-ITA 41, 2007) with the least multipliers for those bounds (checked exactly in `fast_special` tests; the test also runs ten of the phase's hard cases, operands whose quick `(zh, zl)` lies on or within 2^-12 ulp of a midpoint with the exact value on its other side, found by a 2^28-operand search: about 1 in 69000 operands). Profile before (Zen 1 build host, instructions per call, Liella / glibc): FMA erf table 162 / 159, SSE2 235 / 174 (the SSE2 build ran four Dekker products and a degree-14 chain). Not in this decision: `erfc` above 1 (`e^(−x²)·Y`), `erf`'s series below `2^-5`, lgamma/tgamma and the Bessel functions (LIBM-F64-SPECIAL-QUICK-2). (Amended by D-10.90.) |
| D-10.85 | §10.3 | — | **`_Float128` `sinf128`/`cosf128` integer tier: method and proof** (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT; D-10.52's three-limb kernel; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). `crates/math/src/wide_int/quad.rs`, reached through `wide_int::sin_cos` for the 113-bit format from `wide::sin`/`wide::cos`; operands it does not decide take the 384-bit route as before. Method: Payne-Hanek reduction (Payne and Hanek, SIGNUM Newsletter 18(1), 1983) on a 448-bit window of the shared `TWO_OVER_PI` table (exact `m·W mod 2^448`, 13 products), Tang's table method (Tang, ARITH 10, 1991) with 64 points `jπ/256` (the x87 tier's 128-bit `SC` table plus a signed third limb, one table for both formats) and fixed-point Horner in 64-, 128- and 192-bit words (Brent and Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010, ch. 4): degree 15 for `sin(πd/2)`, 14 for `cos(πd/2)`, `\|d\| <= 1/256`. Proof in the module documentation: within `2^-156` relative; the integer rounding test on the 192-bit significand assumes `2^-152` (about `2^-37` of operands undecided). Operands with `\|d\| < 2^-160` are refused (none among the near multiples of π/2 found by the continued-fraction sweep: closest `\|f\|` about `2^-124`). The kernels are not shared with x87 `long double`: that one needs two limbs, and a three-limb kernel would cost it about half again. Tests: constants pinned against the 384-bit arithmetic, the rounding boundary pinned in four modes, agreement with the 384-bit route (1 200 random operands and the near multiples at every 61st exponent in the unit run; 10^7 operands in four modes and every exponent's near multiple in `tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route_long`). Measurements: `handoff/libm-f128-trig-int.md`. |
| D-10.89 | §10.3 | — | **`sincos`, `sincosf`, `sincosl`: one argument reduction for both results** (LIBM-SINCOS-SHARED). Method: sine and cosine of `x = k·(π/2)/2^t + r` come from the same reduced `r` and the same table entries, the cosine by the quadrant shift `k + 2^t` (J.-M. Muller, *Elementary Functions: Algorithms and Implementation*, 3rd ed., 2016, ch. 11, range reduction shared between sin and cos; Cody–Waite and Payne–Hanek reductions as in D-10.52 and D-10.67). Each result is computed by exactly the operations its single function performs on the same values, so `sincos*` returns the bits and flags of `sin*`/`cos*`: correctly rounded in every rounding mode (the bound of the single functions: the rounding tests of Ziv's strategy, with the accurate fallbacks), so at most 0.5 ulp. A result that differs from another library by 1 ulp is within this bound. `float`: the export takes an in-place fast entry, `mret::sincos_fast` with `hot::sincosf_nearest` → `fast32::sincos_nearest_widen` (one `trig_core_with` call, D-10.67/D-10.79, both results rounded by the same test as `sinf`/`cosf`; either refusal sends the call to the cold fallback); before, it went through the full `mret::sincos` envelope on every call. `double`: the in-place tier already shared one reduction (`sincos_tiered`); the envelope path's `trig::sincos` now takes `fast::sincos` (one `kernel::reduce`, one `kernel::poly`, two `assemble`s) and one double-double `sin_cos` for whichever results the fast tier leaves. x87 `long double`: `wide::sincos` takes `wide_int::sin_cos_pair`, which runs steps 1–2 of the integer tier once (`reduced`) and evaluates the sine and cosine series once each, `place` assembling either result exactly as `kernel` does (`kernel` is now `reduced` + `place`), and one 384-bit `sin_cos_of` for whichever results the tier refuses. NaN, ±∞, ±0 and the tiny operands take each single function's own short path. `_Float128`: `sin_cos_pair` takes D-10.91's shared `quad::sin_and_cos`, and the single-function `quad::sin_cos` for both results where that declines (LIBM-SINCOS-SHARED-2, merging next). Tests: `s10_3_c_r4` (sincos against sin and cos, every mode, both formats, every path), `math_float_sincos_fast_entry_matches_the_envelope_in_every_mode`, the exhaustive `sinf_fast_path_agrees_exhaustively` (sincosf against sinf/cosf, every operand and mode) and the `elem_ld_products` sincosl rows. |
| D-10.90 | §10.3 | — | **`erf` (`double`) in-place entry: branch and sign shape** (LIBM-F64-SPECIAL-QUICK-REST, ratchet after D-10.84's SSE2 `erf_series` +1). `fast_special::erf_nearest` tests `ax >= SMALL` (quick phase and table fallback in the taken arm, the `2^-5` series in the else arm): the ordered `>=` compares `ax` with the constant in memory, while `ax < SMALL` first loads the constant into a register. The result's sign is applied by OR-ing `x`'s sign bit into the positive `erf \|x\|` (`with_sign_of`), in place of the compare-and-blend that `if x < 0.0 { -v } else { v }` compiles to on SSE2; the value is the same for every operand the entry reaches (`x` is neither zero nor NaN there, `erf \|x\| > 0`). `erf_quick` uses the same helper. Found by diffing the SSE2 disassembly of the boundary's `erf_nearest` against the revision before D-10.84's change: the `<` compare, `x` held in `xmm13` (a move in and a move out) and the 7-instruction blend. Measured (Skylake-SP build host, `instructions:u` per call, `wl_percall`, `validation/percall/libm_erf.c`; glibc / before D-10.84 / next / this row): SSE2 (`glibc.cpu.hwcaps=-FMA`) `erf_series` 63.0 / 153.0 / 154.0 / **151.0**, `erf_table` 174.0 / 235.0 / 148.0 / **146.0**; FMA `erf_series` 63.0 / 109.0 / 97.0 / 97.0, `erf_table` 159.3 / 162.0 / 120.0 / 120.0; the `erfc` rows unchanged. Tests: `crates/boundary/tests/erf_quick.rs` (both builds, both signs, the series region `0.03..2^-5`); plants `handoff/LIBM-F64-SPECIAL-QUICK-REST-plants.txt`. |
| D-10.91 | §10.3 | — | **`_Float128` `tanf128`/`sincosf128` on the integer tier: one reduction, a Newton quotient** (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-2; extends D-10.85's three-limb kernel; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). `crates/math/src/wide_int/quad.rs`: `both` runs D-10.85's reduction and polynomials once and gives `sin\|a\|` and `cos\|a\|`; `sin_and_cos` (from `wide::sincos` for the 113-bit format) rounds each with the shared integer rounding test, and a function the test does not decide alone takes the 384-bit route; `tan` (from `wide_int::arc::tan`) divides them (`tan a` in even quadrants, `cot a` in odd ones). The quotient `div3`: one `divsd` reciprocal estimate, one Newton step on the reciprocal and one exact residual correction in integer limbs (Brent and Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010, ch. 3; J.-M. Muller, Elementary Functions, 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 2), no integer `div`: within `2^-162.2` relative. Proof (module documentation, steps 6 and 7): `tan` within `2^-155.6`, inside the rounding test's `2^-152`. `sinf128`/`cosf128` keep their single-function kernel (cheaper than computing both). Tests: `quotient_meets_its_bound` (20 000 random significands and the extremes, including `δ = 1/2` where the Newton step is zero and just above it where it is negative), and tan and sincos on every operand of the sin/cos agreement tests (unit and the 10^7 `tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route_long`). Measurements: `handoff/libm-f128-trig-int-2.md`. |
| D-10.92 | §10.3 | — | **`_Float128` sin/cos kernel: the reduction window written out, so sharing the reduction costs sin/cos nothing** (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-3; amends D-10.91's code layout only; method, proof and contract D-10.85/D-10.91/D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode). Cause, from a one-call trace of `sinf128` (validation/wl_trace.sh) and the disassembly of the products before and after D-10.91: once `reduce` had three callers (`kernel`, `both`, `tan_kernel`), the 2/π window `core::array::from_fn(\|k\| ...)` in `reduce` stayed an out-of-line `core::array::try_from_fn` call of about 150 instructions, and with the helpers left to the inliner `kernel` also called `reduce`, `sin_poly`, `cos_poly` and `mulhi3` (five sites) out of line. `crates/math/src/wide_int/quad.rs` now builds the seven window words as an array literal, and `mulhi3`, `mul32`, `sin_poly`, `cos_poly`, `word` and `reduce` are `#[inline(always)]`, so every caller gets one straight-line function whatever the number of callers. Measured (wl_percall, `validation/percall/libm_f128_trig.c`, instructions:u per call, Zen 1 host; before D-10.91 / D-10.91 / now): sinf128 1257 / 1332 / 1253, cosf128 1257 / 1332 / 1253, tanf128 89 475 / 1749 / 1704, sincosf128 2439 / 1831 / 1785 (glibc 7251, 7248, 8173, 8756). Each half alone does not do it: the pins without the window fix measured sinf128 1375 (the window call stayed), the window fix without the pins 1325 (tanf128 1743, sincosf128 1825). Tests: `wide_int::quad` unit tests and the 10^7-operand `tier_agrees_with_the_wide_route_long` in the four modes; plants handoff/LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-3-plants.txt. |
| D-10.95 | §10.3 | — | **Float-to-integer conversions in the math kernels cannot raise invalid** (LIBM-INVALID-CONVERT-SCAN, -2, -3). On x86-64 without AVX-512 an `as u64`/`as i64` of a value at or past 2^63 (or a NaN) is a signed `cvttsd2si` that raises invalid in hardware; under the envelope the flag is then cleared with an MXCSR write, a serialising instruction paid on every call. The `long double` arc kernels (`asinl`, `acosl` on every call; `atan2l`'s quotient seed for a power-of-two divisor) converted values in [2^62, 2^64], and the binary128 `tan` kernel's quotient seed (`tanf128`, `wide_int::quad::div3`) reaches 2^63 when the divisor's top word is below 2^63 + 2^11: `wide_int::big_u64` now reads such a value from the double's bits at all five sites (same result, no conversion instruction). `lgammaf`'s sign (`signgam`) is no longer the parity of an integer conversion: the fast path takes it from the sign of Γ(x) its last branch computes (exact: every factor x + j is exact and nonzero, the fit P > 0; every other branch has x > 0), and the accurate path is unchanged. A clamp before an `as i32` (-2) cost 13 instructions a call on positive operands (per-call count 315.8 to 328.8), reading trunc(x)'s low bit from the float's bits (-3) cost 3; the sign of Γ(x) runs no parity code on the positive path (-4). Every other float-to-integer cast states its operand range in a `RANGE:` comment, and the static check `float-casts` (clippy's cast lints forced on, found by type) fails on a cast in liella-math or `crates/core/src/num/parse.rs` without one or a clamp. Test: `crates/boundary/tests/math_kernel_no_invalid.rs` calls the arc kernels and the binary128 `tan` kernel (operands around 2π/3, where the divisor is sin(π/6) = 1/2) between `feclearexcept` and `fetestexcept`. The strto* converters raise no overflow, underflow or deliberate inexact flag today (probe a7fa43af9749: the reference raises each as IEEE 754 §7 says); that is a separate change (handoff/libm-invalid-convert-scan.md). |
| D-10.96 | §10.3 | — | **`_Float128` `atan`/`atan2`: a three-limb integer first tier (Tang's table, exact numerator and denominator, the binary128 quotient `div3`), proved within `2^-160` relative and rounded by the binary128 rounding test** (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-4; extends D-10.85/D-10.91 to the inverse functions; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode, the 384-bit route settles what the test cannot decide). Before: every `atanf128`/`atan2f128` call took the 384-bit route (about 161 000 and 169 000 instructions, 27x and 24x glibc time on Ivy Bridge). Method (`crates/math/src/wide_int/quad/arc.rs`): the x87 arc kernel (D-10.52, D-10.75) carried to three 64-bit limbs. `atan(y/x)` for `0 < y <= x`: `j = round(128t)` from a `double` estimate (in range: `h` in `[128, 512)`), `atan(y/x) = atan(j/128) + atan(r)`, `r = (y − cx)/(x + cy)` with the numerator and denominator exact integers on the 113-bit significands (the denominator's carry kept as a 129th bit), the quotient by `div3` (Newton's reciprocal and one residual correction, within `2^-162.2`), and `atan r = r·P(r²)` with ten terms of the odd series (remainder `< 2^-164.3`) by Horner in 64-, 128- and 192-bit words. The table is the x87 tier's 128-bit `atan(j/128)` plus a signed third limb (one 1 KB table, not a second 3 KB one). `atan x = A(\|x\|, 1)` or `π/2 − A(1, \|x\|)`; `atan2` the same on `(\|y\|, \|x\|)` then `π − θ` for `x < 0`. Error budget (module documentation): the series steps `λ_6 u^6` (`2^-162.4`) and `λ_2 u^2` (`2^-161.4`) dominate, `P` within `2^-160.69`, every result within `2^-160.2`; the rounding test assumes `2^-152` (B shared with sin/cos/tan). References: P. T. P. Tang, "Table-lookup algorithms for elementary functions and their error analysis", ARITH 10, 1991; R. Brent, P. Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, 2010, ch. 3-4; J.-M. Muller, Elementary Functions, 3rd ed. 2016, ch. 2. Constants from Python `decimal` at 220 digits (π by Machin), pinned against the 384-bit arithmetic by `constants_are_the_rounded_values`. Measured (instructions:u per call, glibc / before / after, `validation/percall/libm_f128_trig.c`): `atanf128` on [-10, 10] 5870 / 161 186 / 1076, on [-1, 1] 5854 / 157 326 / 1033, `atan2f128` 6221 / 168 732 / 1267. `quad::div3` is pinned `#[inline(always)]`: with the arc tier's callers it went out of line and `tanf128` rose 1703.5 -> 1721.5; pinned, every sin/cos/tan/sincos row is at its earlier count. Accuracy: 10^7 seeded operands (half `atan`, half `atan2`) in the four modes against the 384-bit route and the hard cases (`\|x\| = 1` and neighbours, `t` on every index boundary `(2j+1)/256` and one place either side, `t` near 1 and `2^-8`, the extreme and subnormal operands, the denominator carry). `asinf128`/`acosf128` stay on the 384-bit route (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-5): their `√(1 − a²)` has 192 significant bits, so the kernel needs a variant whose `x` is a three-limb value and a three-limb root. |
| D-10.97 | §10.3 | — | **`_Float128` `asin`/`acos`: the three-limb integer first tier through the `atan2` route (exact `1 − a²`, a 192-bit root, D-10.96's kernel on 192-bit operands), proved within `2^-160.2` relative and rounded by the binary128 rounding test** (LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-5/-6; extends D-10.96 to the inverse sine and cosine; contract D-10.19 unchanged: correctly rounded in every mode, the 384-bit route settles what the test cannot decide). Method: `asin a = atan(a/√(1 − a²))`, `acos a = atan(√(1 − a²)/a)` (composed with `π` for `a < 0`), with `1 − a²` exact (`A²` in 256 bits), the root from a correctly rounded `double` square root (`sqrtsd` at the boundary, as the `long double` rows) refined by one 128-bit and one 192-bit Newton step with the reciprocal refined once (`2^-98.8`), the root within `2^-186`; then Tang's table method on the numerator and denominator (`y − cx`, `x + cy` on the 192-bit significands) and the binary128 quotient. A direct `asin` kernel (Taylor centres with their own coefficients) was rejected: about 20 terms of 192 bits per centre (tens of KB of table) and a root needed above `1/2` anyway. Proof in `crates/math/src/wide_int/quad/arc.rs` steps 7-9 (module doc). Evidence: unit tests, 21 120 hard cases and a 10^7 release sweep with 0 undecided, worst error `2^-161.36`; plants in handoff/LIBM-F128-TRIG-INT-6-plants.txt. Sources (specifications): P. T. P. Tang, "Table-lookup algorithms for elementary functions and their error analysis", ARITH 10 (1991); R. P. Brent and P. Zimmermann, Modern Computer Arithmetic, ch. 3-4 (Newton iteration for the root and reciprocal); J.-M. Muller, Elementary Functions, ch. 2 (argument reduction and error analysis). |
| D-10.99 | §10.5 | — | **`cexp` gets a middle tier between its quick tier and the 384-bit route** (LIBM-CEXP-ROUTE, under D-10.53 and D-10.55). When the quick tier's rounding test cannot decide a part of `cexp` (`double`), that part alone is evaluated again with a proved bound near `2^-99` and rounded by the same interval test (`fast64::settle`) in every mode; only a part still undecided reaches the route, unchanged. Why: the quick tier's bound (about `2^-66` relative) leaves about one part in a thousand undecided, and each costed about 115k instructions in the route; the one such operand of cbench_libm's 256 (`(-1.609657171678382, -1.9221928333335072)`, real part `2^-70.3` relative from a midpoint) added about 450 instructions to the row's per-call average. It is not a hard case for correct rounding, only for the quick bound. Method: `e^x` from the double-double kernel of the wide formats (`wide_dd::exp_dd`, `2^-100` relative); `sin y` or `cos y` from a Cody–Waite reduction by `π/2` in three `double`s (exact `two_prod`s, double-double additions) and Taylor series in double-double by Horner's rule, within `2^-100` absolute; the double-double product. Error bounds of the double-double operations: Joldes, Muller and Popescu, ACM TOMS 44(2), 2017; argument-reduction worst case: J.-M. Muller, "Elementary Functions", 3rd ed., 2016. The proof is the comment above `sin_or_cos` in `crates/math/src/complex_fast.rs`. Both builds of the quick tier (baseline, FMA) call the same out-of-line baseline code, so they stay bit-identical. `cexpf` is unchanged. |
| D-10.101 | §10.3 | — | **`sqrt` and `sqrtf` read no MXCSR on entry: `sqrtsd`/`sqrtss` run on the caller's own word under every environment** (LIBM-ENV-CHECK-COST, #4872; amends D-10.71 and the unmasked-trap clause of D-10.22). Cost of the entry check (`stmxcsr`, load, mask, compare, branch), TSC ticks per iteration, best of 7, measured with a loop probe: Zen 1 (EPYC, 60 vCPU) 23.8 for the check alone against 3.1 for the empty loop, so about 21 ticks of reciprocal throughput; `sqrtsd` alone 8.2, with the check 24.5; `sqrtss` 5.1, with the check 24.3. Broadwell-EP 1.2 and Skylake-SP 0.0 for the check (`sqrtss` +0.9 on both, `sqrtsd` +0). In a dependent chain (latency-bound) the check costs nothing on any of the three. On Zen 1 the check is therefore the throughput floor of every short entry that has it (the reference's `sqrt` 11.3, `expf` 12.2, `logf` 12.4, `tanhf` 14.6, `exp` 21.0 ticks per call there); on the Intel classes it is noise. Options weighed: (a) a per-thread "environment is default" byte kept by every fenv path and thread start, letting the default case skip `stmxcsr`: rejected, because MXCSR is ordinary user state that code outside the library writes (inline `ldmxcsr`, `setcontext` and a signal frame's saved word restored by `sigreturn`, a handler's `fesetround(FE_TONEAREST)` landing between an interrupted `fesetround`'s flag store and its `ldmxcsr`), and a stale byte returns round-to-nearest results in another mode, or runs arithmetic under an unmasked trap; no protocol keeps a cache of a register that any instruction may write exact. (c) Detecting the mode with arithmetic (one `addpd` whose two lanes round differently in each direction, a subnormal lane for FTZ/DAZ) costs about three pipelined instructions but cannot see the exception masks and raises inexact in the caller's word: rejected. (b) Read MXCSR only where the fast path's result depends on it: adopted where the hardware operation is itself the specified result in every environment. `sqrtsd`/`sqrtss` are correctly rounded in the current direction (IEEE 754 squareRoot, Intel SDM), read a subnormal operand as a zero of its sign under DAZ, are never affected by FTZ (a non-zero root is normal), and raise exactly the operation's flags, so in place they honour any word however it was set: fenv, a direct `ldmxcsr`, a new thread (which starts with its creator's word), a signal handler's word. An unmasked exception traps in the instruction, before the EDOM store, which is what the reference's `sqrt`/`sqrtf` do (black-box probe, glibc 2.39: invalid for -1 and -inf, inexact for 2, denormal-operand for a subnormal, each trapping with errno untouched; with invalid unmasked and DAZ on, `sqrt(-subnormal)` = -0 and no trap). The previous software fallback under an unmasked exception differed from the reference in four of those cases (no denormal trap and no denormal-operand flag; an invalid trap for `sqrt(-subnormal)` under DAZ); it is gone. Every other fast entry (`elem_fast`, `elem32_fast`, `sincos_fast`) keeps its read: its round-to-nearest result depends on the mode. The `float` functions can drop the read the way D-10.63's one-pass entries do (an evaluation in `double` that is right in every direction and refuses before any operation that could raise more than inexact); that is per-function error analysis, left to follow-up stories. Tests: `math_sqrt_runs_in_place_under_every_mask` (masks a square root never raises, every direction, subnormal operands), `conformance/c/s10_sqrt_env.c` (fesetround, inline `ldmxcsr` with FTZ/DAZ, a new thread per direction, a signal handler changing direction, unmasked traps and their errno). Plants: `handoff/LIBM-ENV-CHECK-COST-plants.txt`. |
